The miner asserted '7-day' without ever establishing the window's alignment — which matters, because 2026-05-17 sitting at acuteDistance 0 exactly 7 days after the 05-10 marathon is what pins the boundary.

History `tolerance` lags PIT `acuteTolerance`. Reported as one shared series; it is two, and the History one is stale. Listed above as a correction but it belongs here too — it is a schema fact the miner never tested.

A 6.092 km HIKING activity on 2026-09-05 (activityId 24245302199, High Peak) and a 3.754 km hike on 2026-07-03 carry real mechanical load and are invisible to running tolerance. The 'only 4.835 km and 10 km treadmill in the last week' picture omits a 6 km hike on the same day as the treadmill run.

MetricsAcuteTrainingLoad_*.json is listed as read but essentially unmined: 269 rows spanning 2026-03-28..2026-09-07 with dailyTrainingLoadAcute, dailyTrainingLoadChronic, dailyAcuteChronicWorkloadRatio and acwrStatus — a complete daily ATL/CTL/ACWR series that is far more directly comparable to rocket's own CTL/ATL/TSB engine than the tolerance metric is. Exactly one number (228) was extracted from it.

The proposed gate `planned_km x 1185 <= tolerance` compares a RAW calendar-week total against a ceiling Garmin calibrates against a DECAYED ~10-day rolling load. The miner documents that gap in unitTraps (2026-08-22: 47,732 decayed vs 52,920 raw, ~10% apart) and then writes a gate that ignores it, making the gate ~10% stricter than Garmin's own rule. The 2.9x headline survives; the gate specification does not.

The file named ...20260706_20261014... contains no data after 2026-09-07. The 2026-10-14 suffix is an export window label, not data extent. Never stated — a reader could reasonably assume forward-dated rows exist.

Neither summarizedActivities nor either tolerance file was cross-checked for the 2 duplicate PIT rows before per-row statistics were computed, which is what produced the 40-of-147 and phrase-count errors. The dedupe advice was written but not applied to the miner's own numbers.

Unexamined and potentially load-bearing for the same domain: EnduranceScore_*, HillScore_*, TrainingHistory_*, TrainingReadinessDTO_* (which also contains acwr fields), RunRacePredictions_* (directly relevant to the 4:45/km half-marathon pacing question), and DI-Connect-Fitness/..._weekly_training_report.json.

domains.title: Training readiness, sleep and health status

mined.domain: Training readiness, sleep and health status (Garmin GDPR export, 2026-09-08)
mined.recordCounts: READINESS: 267 records total (148 in the 20260328_20260706 file + 119 in the 20260706_20261014 file), covering 160 distinct calendarDate values from 2026-03-28 to 2026-09-07 (1-6 records per day; the DTO is written on every wake/post-exercise/realtime-variable event, not once per day). Only 145 of 267 records carry a `score` field at all, spanning 68 distinct days from 2026-06-28 to 2026-09-07. Within that 72-day span exactly 4 days are missing (2026-08-29, 08-30, 08-31, 09-01 — watch not worn), so scored-day coverage is 68/72 = 94.4%. The 92 days from 2026-03-28 to 2026-06-27 have DTO records but NO score (level="NONE", feedback="UNKNOWN", every factor percent 0) — the Training Readiness feature was not yet active. SLEEP: 2 (two) scored nights in the entire export. File 2026-02-21_2026-06-01 has 66 array entries of which 0 are sleep sessions (63 are the bare placeholder {"retro":false}, 3 carry only a napList). File 2026-06-01_2026-09-09 has 97 entries of which exactly 2 are sleep sessions (2026-06-25 and 2026-07-18), 2 are nap-only (2026-09-02, 2026-09-05), 93 are bare placeholders. File 2025-04-27_2025-08-05 is 17 bytes containing the literal `[{"retro":false}]` — one placeholder, zero nights; it is effectively empty. Across the ~194 calendar days nominally covered by the two 2026 sleep files, overnight sleep coverage is 2/194 = 1.0%. HEALTH STATUS: 2 records, calendarDate 2026-06-25 and 2026-07-18 — the same two dates as the two sleep nights, not an independent series. NAPS: 5 total (2026-04-11 720s, 2026-04-17 1440s, 2026-04-21 960s, 2026-09-02 3360s, 2026-09-05 1020s).
mined.schemaNotes: TrainingReadinessDTO — JSON array of objects, 25-29 fields each (optional fields absent, not null). Fields: userProfilePK (int, constant 144449296); calendarDate (str "YYYY-MM-DD"); timestamp / timestampLocal (str ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.f", NOT epoch ms — this differs from summarizedActivities.json; timestampLocal is timestamp +1h through the whole file, i.e. Europe/London BST); deviceId (int, constant 3613943939 — single device); score (int 1-94 observed, ABSENT on 122/267 records); level (str enum: NONE / POOR / LOW / MODERATE / HIGH — observed bands map exactly to score: POOR 1-23, LOW 25-49, MODERATE 50-74, HIGH 75-94; Garmin's PRIME band never occurs); feedbackLong (str, 17 distinct enum keys e.g. HIGH_RT_AVAILABLE_SS_UNKNOWN, LOW_RT_MOD_OR_LOW_SS_UNKNOWN_ACWR_NEG); feedbackShort (str, 13 distinct e.g. WELL_RECOVERED, LET_YOUR_BODY_RECOVER, RECOVERY_IN_PROGRESS, HIGH_RECOVERY_NEEDS, BOOSTED_BY_NAPPING, ENERGIZING_NAP, RESTED_AND_READY, GOOD_SLEEP_HISTORY, BOOSTED_BY_LIGHTER_TRAINING); recoveryTime (int, MINUTES — verified below — floor 1, ceiling 5760 = 96h = 4 days); acuteLoad (int, unitless Garmin acute training load 0-1008, ABSENT on 9 records); validSleep (bool); inputContext (str enum: AFTER_WAKEUP_RESET / AFTER_POST_EXERCISE_RESET / UPDATE_REALTIME_VARIABLES); recoveryTimeChangePhrase (str, present on 63/267 only: NAP, NEW_EXERCISE, NO_CHANGE_SLEEP, POOR_SLEEP_RT_LOW, REACHED_ZERO, VERY_HIGH_RELAXATION); sleepScore (int, present on 3/267 records only). SIX FACTOR PAIRS, each `<name>FactorPercent` (int 0-100, 0 = inactive) + `<name>FactorFeedback` (str enum NONE/POOR/MODERATE/GOOD/VERY_GOOD, NONE = inactive): sleepScoreFactor, recoveryTimeFactor, acwrFactor (acute:chronic workload ratio), stressHistoryFactor, hrvFactor, sleepHistoryFactor. Plus hrvWeeklyAverage (float). Higher factor percent = better; the readiness score is dragged down by the LOWEST active factor. sleepData — JSON array; the overwhelming majority of entries are the two-byte-payload placeholder {"retro": false} carrying no date and no data (a night with no recording). A real sleep entry has: calendarDate, sleepStartTimestampGMT / sleepEndTimestampGMT (str ISO-8601, NOT epoch ms, GMT despite the athlete being on BST), sleepWindowConfirmationType (str, "ENHANCED_CONFIRMED_FINAL"), deepSleepSeconds / lightSleepSeconds / remSleepSeconds / awakeSleepSeconds / unmeasurableSeconds (int SECONDS, all quantised to 60s multiples), averageRespiration / lowestRespiration / highestRespiration (float, breaths/min), avgSleepStress (float 0-100 Garmin stress scale), awakeCount (int), restlessMomentCount (int), retro (bool), and a nested sleepScores object with 12 int subscores 0-100 (overallScore, qualityScore, durationScore, recoveryScore, deepScore, remScore, lightScore, awakeningsCountScore, awakeTimeScore, combinedAwakeScore, restfulnessScore, interruptionsScore) plus feedback (str enum) and insight (str enum). A nap-only entry has just {napList: [{napTimeSec (int SECONDS), napStartTimestampGMT, napEndTimestampGMT, calendarDate}], retro}. healthStatusData — JSON array; each object: calendarDate, createTimestampUTC / updateTimestampUTC (ISO-8601), outliersCount (int), metrics (array of 5 objects, one per type HRV / HR / SPO2 / SKIN_TEMP_C / RESPIRATION, each with value (float, ABSENT for SPO2 and SKIN_TEMP_C), baselineUpperLimit / baselineLowerLimit (float), status (str: ONBOARDING or UNKNOWN), percentage (float), feedbackKey (str)).

findings.claim: recoveryTime is in MINUTES, not hours or seconds, with a hard ceiling of 5760 (= 96 h = 4 days) and a floor of 1
findings.value: minutes; range 1-5760
findings.derivation: TrainingReadinessDTO_*.json. Derived two independent ways. (1) Wall-clock decay: for consecutive records with no intervening exercise/nap reset, (recoveryTime[n] - recoveryTime[n+1]) / (timestamp[n+1] - timestamp[n] in minutes) = 0.998-0.999 across 10 clean pairs, e.g. 2026-03-30T07:19:50 -> 2026-03-31T07:24:50 is 1445.0 min elapsed and recoveryTime drops 1444 (ratio 0.999; the sub-1.0 is second-level truncation, not a different unit). (2) Ceiling: max observed value is exactly 5760 across 267 records = 96 h, matching Garmin's documented 4-day recovery-time cap. Seconds would make the cap 96 min; hours would make it 240 days. Both absurd.

findings.claim: hrvWeeklyAverage is a dead constant and must not be ingested — it is 511.0 on every single record including days before any HRV was ever measured
findings.value: 511.0 on 267/267 records (0 distinct alternative values)
findings.derivation: TrainingReadinessDTO_*.json, field hrvWeeklyAverage: set(r['hrvWeeklyAverage'] for r in recs) == {511.0} over all 267 records spanning 2026-03-28 to 2026-09-07. It is present and identical on 2026-03-28, the first record, when hrvFactorPercent=0 and hrvFactorFeedback='NONE'. Corroborating: hrvFactorPercent is 0 and hrvFactorFeedback is 'NONE' on 267/267 records, i.e. HRV never once contributed to a readiness score. Tempting misreading: 511.0 as deci-milliseconds -> 51.1 ms, which is plausibly near the 59/67 ms in healthStatusData. Do not do this — a value that never changes across 163 days is a placeholder, not a measurement.

findings.claim: Only 2 nights of overnight sleep exist in the entire export. There is no sleep series.
findings.value: 2 nights: 2026-06-25 and 2026-07-18. Earliest 2026-06-25, latest 2026-07-18. Nothing before, nothing after (54 days of nothing up to the 2026-09-08 export).
findings.derivation: Counted entries carrying a 'sleepScores' key across all three sleepData files. 2025-04-27_2025-08-05: 1 entry, [{"retro":false}], 0 nights. 2026-02-21_2026-06-01: 66 entries, 0 with sleepScores (63 bare placeholders, 3 napList-only). 2026-06-01_2026-09-09: 97 entries, 2 with sleepScores (array index 24 -> 2026-06-25, index 47 -> 2026-07-18), 2 napList-only, 93 bare placeholders. Total 2. Independently corroborated in the readiness DTO: validSleep is True on only 3 of 267 records, on exactly 2 distinct dates (2026-06-26 and 2026-07-18), and sleepScore appears on only those same 3 records with values 56 and 95 — matching the two nights' overallScore of 56 and 95 exactly.

findings.claim: Night 1 (2026-06-25): 4.68 h in bed, 4.27 h asleep, sleep score 56
findings.value: window 16860 s = 4.68 h; asleep 15360 s = 4.27 h; overallScore 56, durationScore 38
findings.derivation: 2026-06-01_2026-09-09_144449296_sleepData.json. Two independent derivations agree exactly. (1) Timestamp window: sleepEndTimestampGMT 2026-06-26T03:13:28 minus sleepStartTimestampGMT 2026-06-25T22:32:28 = 16860 s. (2) Stage sum: deep 3660 + light 9120 + rem 2580 + awake 1500 + unmeasurable 0 = 16860 s. Delta = 0 s exactly. Asleep excludes awake and unmeasurable: 16860 - 1500 - 0 = 15360 s = 4.27 h. Other fields: averageRespiration 14.53, avgSleepStress 6.36, awakeCount 1, restlessMomentCount 19, feedback POSITIVE_SHORT_BUT_RECOVERING.

findings.claim: Night 2 (2026-07-18): 9.98 h in bed, 9.72 h asleep, sleep score 95
findings.value: window 35916 s = 9.98 h; asleep 34980 s = 9.72 h; overallScore 95, durationScore 100
findings.derivation: Same file. (1) Timestamp window: 2026-07-18T09:12:27 minus 2026-07-17T23:13:51 = 35916 s. (2) Stage sum: deep 4500 + light 21600 + rem 8880 + awake 0 + unmeasurable 960 = 35940 s. Delta = +24 s, i.e. the stage sum overshoots the window by 24 s because stages are quantised to 60 s multiples. Use the timestamp window as authoritative for duration. Asleep = 35940 - 0 - 960 = 34980 s = 9.72 h. Other fields: averageRespiration 16.4, avgSleepStress 4.63, awakeCount 0, restlessMomentCount 47, feedback POSITIVE_HIGHLY_RECOVERING.

findings.claim: HRV exists as exactly 2 point-in-time values, both explicitly flagged ONBOARDING by Garmin with zero-width baselines — Garmin itself declines to interpret them
findings.value: HRV 59.0 ms (2026-06-25) and 67.0 ms (2026-07-18); status ONBOARDING on both; baselineUpperLimit = baselineLowerLimit = 0.0 on both; percentage 0.0
findings.derivation: 2026-06-25_2026-07-18_144449296_healthStatusData.json, metrics[] entries with type=='HRV'. The feedbackKey on both is LHA_OFF_YOUR_BASELINE_FEEDBACK_HRV_UNKNOWN. baselineUpperLimit and baselineLowerLimit are both 0.0, meaning no baseline band has been established — Garmin has not yet computed one. Corroborated from the other side: hrvFactorPercent = 0 and hrvFactorFeedback = 'NONE' on 267/267 readiness records, so Garmin's own readiness engine never fed HRV into a score. Unit is milliseconds (rMSSD): 59 and 67 are physiologically normal overnight rMSSD for a trained runner; the readiness DTO's hrvWeeklyAverage of 511.0 is a separate, dead field and is NOT the same quantity.

findings.claim: The health-status file is not a health-condition log — it is a 5-metric off-your-baseline snapshot, and it exists only for the two nights the watch was worn overnight
findings.value: 2 records; window 2026-06-25 to 2026-07-18 (24 calendar days), but only 2 days populated. outliersCount 0 on both.
findings.derivation: 2026-06-25_2026-07-18_144449296_healthStatusData.json. Its two calendarDate values (2026-06-25, 2026-07-18) are identical to the two sleep-session calendarDate values in 2026-06-01_2026-09-09_sleepData.json. The filename's date range is simply first-to-last populated record, not a continuous window. Content is Garmin's 'Health Snapshot / off-your-baseline' feature: HRV 59.0 -> 67.0, resting HR 60.0 -> 53.0 bpm, RESPIRATION 14.5 -> 16.4 breaths/min (all status ONBOARDING), plus SPO2 and SKIN_TEMP_C which have NO value key at all and status UNKNOWN (the sensor produced nothing). outliersCount 0 means no metric was flagged out of band — trivially true since no baselines exist. It is recording no illness or condition.

findings.claim: Readiness is limited by recoveryTime on 62 of 68 scored days. Sleep, HRV and stress are effectively absent as inputs.
findings.value: Limiting factor tally over the 68 scored days: recoveryTime 62, acwr 5, sleepScore 1. Factor-active days: recoveryTime 68/68, acwr 65/68, sleepHistory 3/68, sleepScore 1/68, hrv 0/68, stressHistory 0/68.
findings.derivation: TrainingReadinessDTO_*.json. For each of the 68 days carrying a score, took the last scored record of the day, treated a factor as active when its <name>FactorFeedback != 'NONE', and took the limiting factor as the active factor with the lowest <name>FactorPercent. sleepScoreFactorPercent is non-zero on exactly one day (2026-07-18, 95%) and sleepHistoryFactorPercent on exactly three (2026-06-28 at 38%, 2026-07-19 and 2026-07-20 at 95%) — all three trace to the two recorded nights. stressHistoryFactorPercent and hrvFactorPercent are 0 with feedback 'NONE' on all 267 records.

findings.claim: Daily readiness score series is usable from 2026-06-28 onward and nothing before
findings.value: 68 scored days, 2026-06-28 to 2026-09-07, score range 1-94; 4-day hole 2026-08-29 to 2026-09-01. Daily level counts (last scored record of day): HIGH 27, MODERATE 22, POOR 13, LOW 6.
findings.derivation: TrainingReadinessDTO_*.json. Days with >=1 record carrying a score: 68. First 2026-06-28, last 2026-09-07 — a 72-day calendar span with exactly 4 absent days (2026-08-29/30/31, 2026-09-01), giving 94.4% coverage. The 92 preceding days (2026-03-28 to 2026-06-27) carry 122 records with level='NONE', feedbackShort='UNKNOWN' and every factor percent 0 — present in the file but carrying no readiness information. Note: multiple records exist per day (1-6), so any ingest must pick a convention; last-scored-record-of-day gives a 1-94 range, max-of-day gives 4-94 (median 75, mean 67.5).

findings.claim: acuteLoad is a usable independent 7-day-load series, longer than the readiness score series
findings.value: 258 of 267 records carry acuteLoad; range 0-1008; runs from 2026-04-03 to 2026-09-07 (158 days)
findings.derivation: TrainingReadinessDTO_*.json, field acuteLoad. Absent on the 9 earliest records (2026-03-28 to 2026-04-02) then continuously present. It is Garmin's unitless acute training load (a ~7-day exponentially weighted sum of per-session training-load/EPOC values), NOT a distance or duration. A prolonged run of exactly 0 from 2026-05-20 to 2026-06-02 (14 consecutive days) coincides with recoveryTime pinned at its floor of 1 — a genuine 2-week training gap, not missing data.

findings.claim: Nap detection is real and demonstrably feeds the readiness score
findings.value: 5 naps; the two 2026 September naps produce matching readiness feedback on the same day
findings.derivation: Cross-file check. sleepData 2026-06-01_2026-09-09 records napList entries on 2026-09-02 (napTimeSec 3360 = 56 min) and 2026-09-05 (napTimeSec 1020 = 17 min). The readiness DTO's feedbackShort for those exact dates is 'ENERGIZING_NAP' (2026-09-02) and 'BOOSTED_BY_NAPPING' (2026-09-05), and recoveryTimeChangePhrase 'NAP' appears in the record set. Independent files agreeing on both date and semantics confirms the nap plumbing is intact even though overnight sleep is not.

unitTraps: recoveryTime is MINUTES (ceiling 5760 = 96 h = 4 days, floor 1). Reading it as hours gives a 240-day recovery; as seconds gives 96 minutes. Verified by wall-clock decay ratio 0.999 min-per-min across 10 clean consecutive pairs.

Timestamps in BOTH TrainingReadinessDTO and sleepData are ISO-8601 STRINGS ('2026-06-25T22:32:28.0'), NOT epoch milliseconds. This is the opposite convention to summarizedActivities.json in the same export. A parser that assumes epoch ms across the export will crash or silently coerce garbage here.

hrvWeeklyAverage = 511.0 is constant on 267/267 records and is NOT an HRV measurement. It is superficially rescalable to 51.1 ms, which is close enough to the real 59/67 ms in healthStatusData to look convincing. It is a placeholder. Reject the field entirely.

Sleep stage fields are SECONDS and quantised to 60 s. On night 2 the stage sum (35940 s) overshoots the actual sleepStart-to-sleepEnd window (35916 s) by 24 s. Use the timestamp window for duration; the stage sum is not an exact reconstruction.
'Time asleep' is NOT the stage sum. awakeSleepSeconds and unmeasurableSeconds are included in the stage sum and in the bed window. Night 2 is 9.98 h in bed but 9.72 h asleep.

All *FactorPercent fields are 0-100 where HIGHER IS BETTER (a percent of full contribution), and 0 means the factor is INACTIVE, not 'maximally bad'. The paired *FactorFeedback == 'NONE' is the only reliable inactive marker. Treating a 0 percent as a bad sleep or bad HRV reading would invert the meaning on 267 records.

sleepData calendarDate is INCONSISTENT between the two nights: night 1 (bed 2026-06-25 22:32, wake 2026-06-26 03:13) is labelled 2026-06-25 (bedtime date), while night 2 (bed 2026-07-17 23:13, wake 2026-07-18 09:12) is labelled 2026-07-18 (wake date). The readiness DTO, by contrast, is consistently wake-date (it attributes night 1's sleepScore 56 to 2026-06-26). Joining sleep to readiness on calendarDate will mis-key night 1 by one day.

sleep timestamps are suffixed GMT and are genuinely GMT/UTC, while the athlete is on BST (UTC+1) — confirmed because the readiness DTO's timestampLocal is exactly timestamp + 1 h throughout. Night 2's 23:13 GMT bedtime is 00:13 local.
napTimeSec is SECONDS (3360 = 56 min), unlike everything else in the readiness DTO which is minutes.

Filename date ranges are first-to-last populated record, not continuous coverage windows. healthStatusData's '20260625_20260718' contains 2 records, not 24 days. sleepData's '2026-02-21_2026-06-01' contains 0 nights.
dataQualityIssues: Only 2 nights of overnight sleep in the whole export (2026-06-25, 2026-07-18). 1.0% coverage over the ~194 days the 2026 sleep files nominally span. There is no sleep series to speak of.

The 2025-04-27_2025-08-05 sleep file is 17 bytes: the literal [{"retro":false}]. It is one placeholder object with no date, no duration, no stages. Not corrupt — genuinely empty. Do not treat its filename range as 100 days of data.
hrvWeeklyAverage is frozen at 511.0 across every record spanning 163 days. Dead field.
hrvFactorPercent = 0 / hrvFactorFeedback = 'NONE' and stressHistoryFactorPercent = 0 / 'NONE' on 267/267 records. Two of the six documented readiness inputs never fired once.

122 of 267 readiness records (2026-03-28 to 2026-06-27) have no score at all — level 'NONE', feedback 'UNKNOWN', all factors zero. They are structurally valid but informationally empty. A naive ingest that defaults a missing score to 0 would inject 92 days of phantom 'terrible readiness'.
4-day hole in the readiness series: 2026-08-29 through 2026-09-01 inclusive, with no records in either DTO file.

14 consecutive days of acuteLoad == 0 (2026-05-20 to 2026-06-02) with recoveryTime pinned at its floor of 1. This is a real training gap, not a sensor failure — but any ATL/CTL backfill must distinguish 'zero load' from 'no data' here, and the readiness files alone cannot make that distinction.
SPO2 and SKIN_TEMP_C in healthStatusData have no `value` key at all (not null — the key is absent) with status 'UNKNOWN'. A parser doing metric['value'] will KeyError.

Multiple readiness records per calendar day (1 to 6) with no explicit 'final' flag. Any daily series requires an explicit selection convention; last-scored-record-of-day and max-of-day disagree (day-1 score 1 vs 4 on 2026-06-28 and 2026-07-02 respectively).

Array-index-to-date mapping in sleepData is unreliable for the 2026-02-21_2026-06-01 file. Bare {"retro":false} placeholders carry no date, and the three dated nap entries in that file imply index 0 == 2026-03-29 (66 entries ending 2026-06-02), which contradicts the filename's 2026-02-21 start. The 2026-06-01_2026-09-09 file's dated entries DO map cleanly with index 0 == 2026-06-01. Do not reconstruct dates by array position; use only the calendarDate carried inside populated entries.
surprises: The brief anticipated a sparse HRV baseline. Reality is more extreme: there is NO HRV time series file anywhere in the export (a recursive find for *hrv*, *stress*, *respiration* across the whole DI_CONNECT tree returns zero files). HRV exists as exactly two scalar readings inside healthStatusData, and Garmin itself marks both ONBOARDING with zero-width baselines. rocket cannot compute an HRV trend, a baseline, or a deviation — not 'with low confidence', but at all.

Garmin's own readiness engine has never used HRV or stress history as an input for this athlete: hrvFactorPercent and stressHistoryFactorPercent are 0 with feedback 'NONE' on all 267 records. The readiness score is essentially a repackaging of recoveryTime (limiting on 62/68 days) with acwr as a secondary. Anyone treating Garmin readiness as a holistic recovery signal for this athlete is treating a recovery-timer countdown as a physiological measurement.

The healthStatusData file is not an illness or health-event log, which its name suggests. It is the 'off your baseline' 5-metric snapshot, and it contains records ONLY for the two dates that also have sleep sessions — it is derived from overnight wear, not independent.

Readiness scoring did not exist before 2026-06-28, only 72 days ago, despite the DTO records starting 2026-03-28. The first 92 days of the readiness file are structurally present but empty. The usable readiness history is materially shorter than the file date ranges imply.

Naps are recorded and demonstrably influence the readiness score (2026-09-02 'ENERGIZING_NAP', 2026-09-05 'BOOSTED_BY_NAPPING' matching napList entries on the same dates), even though overnight sleep is almost never recorded. The watch is being worn during the day and taken off at night.

The most recent overnight sleep is 2026-07-18 — 52 days before the export and 56 days before race day. The athlete is not currently wearing the watch overnight at all, so the sleep and HRV channels are not merely sparse historically, they are dead right now.
mined.rocketRelevance:
BACKFILL these three, they are dense enough to trust. (1) recoveryTime — 267 records over 160 days (2026-03-28 to 2026-09-07), minutes, floor 1, ceiling 5760. This is the single most complete recovery signal in the domain and it is what actually drives Garmin's readiness on 62 of 68 days. (2) Daily readiness score + level — 68 days, 2026-06-28 to 2026-09-07, 94.4% coverage. Usable, but ingest it labelled as what it is: a recoveryTime countdown, not a physiological readiness measure. (3) acuteLoad — 258 records, 2026-04-03 to 2026-09-07, unitless Garmin 7-day EWMA. Do NOT backfill this into rocket's ATL — it is a different quantity on a different scale from a TSS/TRIMP-based ATL. Use it as an independent CROSS-CHECK: rocket's own ATL should correlate strongly with Garmin acuteLoad in shape; a divergence means rocket's per-session load estimate is wrong. Same for acwrFactorPercent as a sanity check on rocket's TSB sign.

IGNORE outright. hrvWeeklyAverage (constant 511.0, dead field — reject at the parser, do not rescale it to 51.1 ms because it looks plausible). hrvFactorPercent and stressHistoryFactorPercent (0/NONE on 267/267). The 122 unscored readiness records from 2026-03-28 to 2026-06-27 (must be dropped, not defaulted to 0). The 2025 sleep file (17 bytes, empty).

DO NOT SURFACE AN HRV BASELINE. rocket has 2 HRV values, 23 days apart, both flagged ONBOARDING by Garmin with baselineUpperLimit == baselineLowerLimit == 0.0, and the most recent is 2026-07-18 — 52 days stale. Garmin's own threshold for an HRV status is roughly 3 weeks of consecutive overnight wear; this athlete has 2 non-consecutive nights. Any HRV trend, 7-day average, or 'HRV is down, back off' message rocket renders from this would be fabricated. Same for sleep: 2 nights out of ~194.

READINESS-GATED SESSION SWAP — what can drive it. The only defensible gate before the 2026-09-12 half and through the 5-week build is recoveryTime, optionally with the readiness score as a display label. A concrete rule that the data supports: if recoveryTime at the planned session start exceeds the session's planned duration, downgrade the session. This is well-founded because recoveryTime is present on every one of the 160 days and decays deterministically at 1 unit per wall-clock minute, so it can be projected forward to a session time without a model. The readiness score's own bands are directly usable as thresholds (POOR 1-23, LOW 25-49, MODERATE 50-74, HIGH 75-94, verified empirically against 145 scored records) — a swap at score < 50 fires on 19 of the 68 observed days, which is a plausible trigger rate.

SPARSITY THRESHOLD — concrete. Require >= 14 of the trailing 21 days present (>= 67% coverage) before any metric is allowed to drive an automated session swap, and >= 7 of the trailing 14 before it is even displayed with a trend arrow. Against that bar: recoveryTime passes (161/163 days present in the last 21-day window bar the 4-day August hole), readiness score passes (68/72), acuteLoad passes. Sleep scores 0/21 in the trailing window and HRV scores 0/21 — both fail by the widest possible margin and must be rendered as 'not tracked' rather than as an empty chart or a zero. Additionally gate HRV specifically on Garmin's own status field: refuse to display anything while status == 'ONBOARDING' or baselineUpperLimit == 0.0, both of which currently hold.

OPERATIONAL NOTE for the 2026-09-12 race. On the last recorded day, 2026-09-07, readiness was 79 (HIGH), recoveryTime 1 min, acuteLoad 228 and falling from a 2026-08-02 peak of 944 — consistent with a taper. The limiting factor that day was acwr at 95% (GOOD). Nothing in this domain argues against the planned 4:45/km opening. But the 'HR under 170 at 10 km' decision rule depends on live heart rate, not on anything in these six files — resting HR appears here exactly twice (60.0 bpm on 2026-06-25, 53.0 on 2026-07-18) and cannot support a baseline either.

mined.schemaNotes:
RunRacePredictions[] — {userProfilePK: int, calendarDate: str "YYYY-MM-DD" (the day the prediction APPLIES to), deviceId: int, timestamp: str "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.0" (LOCAL time the prediction was computed; note it is usually the PREVIOUS evening ~23:0x for the nightly rollover record), raceTime5K: int, raceTime10K: int, raceTimeHalf: int, raceTimeMarathon: int}. All four raceTime* are WHOLE SECONDS — not ms, not cs. No nulls, no missing fields in any of the 308 records. Typically 1-3 records per calendarDate: one nightly rollover (timestamp = previous day ~22:59-23:05 local) plus one per qualifying run (timestamp = run end). Sort by (calendarDate, timestamp) and take the last row per calendarDate for a daily series.

EnduranceScore[] — {userProfilePK, deviceId, calendarDate: int EPOCH MILLISECONDS at 00:00:00 UTC, timestamp: int epoch ms (compute time, local-shifted), overallScore: int (ABSENT — key missing entirely, not null — for the 13 days 2026-03-28..2026-04-09 before the score first populated), classification: int enum, feedbackPhrase: int enum, primaryTrainingDevice: bool (always true), enduranceScoreContributor: list}. Contributor entries come in TWO INCOMPATIBLE SHAPES in the same array: {group: int, contribution: float} and {sport: int, subSport: int, contribution: float}. A parser that assumes `group` exists will KeyError (it did for me on the first pass). group 0 = running (~95-97%), group 8 = unscored/other (0.00-0.01%), sport 17/subSport 0 = hiking-type contribution (2-5%). Contributions sum to 100.0.

HillScore[] — {userProfilePk (NOTE the lowercase `k` — differs from every other file's userProfilePK), deviceId, calendarDate: int epoch ms, timestamp: int epoch ms, strengthScore: int 0-100, enduranceScore: int 0-100, overallScore: int 0-100, hillScoreClassificationId: int, hillScoreFeedbackPhraseId: int, primaryTrainingDevice: bool}. strengthScore/enduranceScore/overallScore keys are ABSENT for the 14 days 2026-03-28..2026-04-10.

MetricsMaxMetData[] — {userProfilePK, calendarDate: str "YYYY-MM-DD", deviceId, updateTimestamp: str local ISO, sport: "RUNNING" (all 51), subSport: "GENERIC" (all 51), vo2MaxValue: float (integer-valued, the number the watch displays), maxMet: float (full precision, ml/kg/min ÷ 3.5), maxMetCategory: "GENERIC" (all 51), calibratedData: 1 (all 51)}. Verified relation on all 51 records: round(maxMet * 3.5) == vo2MaxValue exactly. Back it out with maxMet for a continuous series; vo2MaxValue alone quantises to 1.0 steps and hides real movement.

unitTraps: raceTime5K / raceTime10K / raceTimeHalf / raceTimeMarathon are WHOLE SECONDS (integers). Not ms. 5905 = 1:38:25. Verified by dividing into distance to get a sane pace (4:39.9/km) and by cross-checking the 5K:HM ratio against Riegel.

RunRacePredictions.calendarDate is a STRING 'YYYY-MM-DD' but EnduranceScore.calendarDate and HillScore.calendarDate are INTEGER EPOCH MILLISECONDS at 00:00:00 UTC. Same conceptual field, two types, in sibling files in the same directory. A shared parser must branch on type.

RunRacePredictions.timestamp is usually the PREVIOUS evening (e.g. calendarDate 2026-09-07 has timestamp 2026-09-06T23:03:42.0). Keying a daily series on `timestamp` rather than `calendarDate` shifts the whole series one day earlier. Use calendarDate for the day, timestamp only to order within a day.

MetricsMaxMetData.vo2MaxValue is a float that only ever holds integers (48.0..53.0) — it is the rounded display value. The real resolution is in maxMet: vo2MaxValue == round(maxMet * 3.5), verified true on all 51 records. Ingesting vo2MaxValue alone quantises away ~1 ml/kg/min of real movement.
HillScore uses `userProfilePk` (lowercase k) where every other file in this domain uses `userProfilePK`. A case-sensitive parser reused across files will KeyError on exactly one of them.

enduranceScoreContributor entries have two mutually exclusive shapes — {group, contribution} and {sport, subSport, contribution}. Both appear inside the SAME array on the same day. Accessing c['group'] unconditionally throws (it threw for me).

overallScore (EnduranceScore) and overallScore/strengthScore/enduranceScore (HillScore) are ABSENT KEYS, not nulls, for the first ~2 weeks of the export. Use .get(), and treat absence as 'not yet computed', not as zero.

CONTRADICTS THE BRIEF: summarizedActivities.avgSpeed is genuinely cm/ms, which is m/s x 10, NOT 'numerically equal to m/s'. Verified on the 2026-09-05 treadmill run: distance 1000000 cm / duration 2953889 ms = 3.385 m/s, and avgSpeed reads 0.3386. So m/s = avgSpeed * 10, and s/km = 100 / avgSpeed. No enum lookup table anywhere in the export for classification, feedbackPhrase, hillScoreClassificationId, hillScoreFeedbackPhraseId, or the contributor sport/group ids. Numeric-to-label mapping is inference from score ranges only.

mined.rocketRelevance:
BACKFILL RunRacePredictions and MetricsMaxMetData; CROSS-CHECK against EnduranceScore; IGNORE HillScore.

1. BACKFILL RunRacePredictions as a daily fitness-oracle series (155 days, 2026-04-03 to 2026-09-07). 2. BACKFILL MetricsMaxMetData with maxMet (not vo2MaxValue) as a slow-moving aerobic-ceiling series, 49 points. It is event-driven, so rocket must forward-fill and label as-of dates, never interpolate.

A divergence is a bug signal in the load engine. Do not backfill it as a load input — it is a Garmin composite whose formula rocket cannot reproduce.

FOR THE RACE IN 4 DAYS (2026-09-12, Battersea Half): Garmin's most recent half prediction, stated exactly, is 5905 seconds = 1:38:25, computed 2026-09-06T23:03:42 local and applying to calendarDate 2026-09-07. corrections: RunRacePredictions has 307 DISTINCT records, not 308 — the two files overlap by one byte-identical record on 2026-07-06 (timestamp 2026-07-05T23:02:51.0, 1175/2504/5762/12993). RunRacePredictions.timestamp and MetricsMaxMetData.updateTimestamp are UTC/GMT, NOT local. Proof: MetricsHeatAltitudeAcclimation carries the same instant twice, as timestamp '2026-09-06T23:03:42.0' and altitudeAcclimationLocalTimestamp '2026-09-07T00:03:42.0'. The consequence is the opposite of what the miner wrote: the nightly rollover record is not 'the previous evening' — it fires at 00:0x LOCAL on the calendarDate it belongs to. A parser that treats this string as local will be one hour out during BST and will mis-describe the rollover.

The RunRacePredictions blackout is THREE days (2026-08-30, 08-31, 09-01), not four. EnduranceScore and HillScore are the ones missing four days (2026-08-29 through 09-01). The finding and the recordCounts section of the same report disagree with each other.

mined.schemaNotes:
UNITS FIRST. weight: grams, float (85500.0 = 85.5 kg) — verified because 85.5/(1.778^2) = 27.046 which equals the stored bmi 27.0459715 to 5 s.f. height: centimetres, float32 artifact (177.8000030517578 = 177.8 cm). All HR fields: integer bpm, no scaling. avgSpeed/maxSpeed/lactateThresholdSpeed: the field value x 10 = m/s — I verified this on 6 activities by computing (distance_cm/100)/(duration_ms/1000) and dividing by the stated avgSpeed; the ratio was 9.9983-10.0015 every time. So lactateThresholdSpeed 0.38333226 means 3.8333 m/s = 4:20.9/km, NOT 0.383 m/s. Power: watts, float, unscaled.

144449296_userBioMetrics.json — list of 85 sparse event objects. Every object has: version (epoch ms, int), metaData{userProfilePK:int, calendarDate:"YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.0", sequence:int == version}, and 9 userSetNullFor* booleans (all false throughout; ignore). Then ONE OR MORE optional payload fields, and which fields appear defines the record type: (a) {vo2MaxRunning:float} alone — the daily VO2max ping, 60 of 85 rows; (b) {height:float} — 2 rows only, both 2026-03-28, 175.0 then 177.8; (c) {weight:{weight:float_grams, sourceType:"USER_SETTING", timestampGMT:"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.mmm"}} — nested object, 2 rows only, both 2026-03-28; (d) {functionalThresholdPower:int, sportId:int} where sportId 1=RUNNING, 2=CYCLING, 12=CROSS_COUNTRY_SKIING; (e) the fat "threshold" row {height, lactateThresholdSpeed:float, lactateThresholdHearRate:int (note the typo — "HearRate", no T), firstbeatRunningLtTimestamp:int, thresholdHeartRateAutoDetected:bool, ftpAutoDetected:bool, vo2MaxRunning}. firstbeatRunningLtTimestamp is a Garmin/FIT epoch (seconds since 1989-12-31), NOT Unix — 1155133851 decodes to 2026-08-08, matching its calendarDate. NO restingHeartRate field exists anywhere in this file.

144449296_bioMetrics_latest.json — single-element list: {lactateThresholdSpeed:0.38333226, lactateThresholdHeartRate:177 (correct spelling here, unlike userBioMetrics), functionalThresholdPower:237}. TRAP: the 237 is the CYCLING FTP; the field is unlabelled by sport.

144449296_userBioMetricProfileData.json — single-element list: {height:177.8, weight:85500.0, vo2Max:53.0, lactateThresholdHeartRate:177.0, functionalThresholdPower:454}. Same unlabelled field name as above but holds the RUNNING FTP. The two "latest" files disagree on functionalThresholdPower (237 vs 454); powerZones.json is the only file that disambiguates by sport.

144449296_heartRateZones.json — single-element list: {trainingMethod:"HR_MAX", restingHeartRateUsed:86, lactateThresholdHeartRateUsed:177, zone1Floor:100, zone2Floor:118, zone3Floor:137, zone4Floor:157, zone5Floor:176, maxHeartRateUsed:196, restingHrAutoUpdateUsed:false, sport:"DEFAULT", changeState:"UNCHANGED"}. No timestamp of any kind. Zone floors are inclusive lower bounds; there is no zone6/zone7 and no explicit ceiling (zone5 runs to maxHeartRateUsed).

144449296_powerZones.json — 3-element list, one per sport: {sport:str, functionalThresholdPower:float, zone1Floor..zone7Floor:float}. RUNNING uses only 5 zones (zone6Floor=zone7Floor=0.0); CYCLING and XC-skiing use 7 with zone1Floor=0.0. A 0.0 floor means "zone unused", not "floor at zero watts" — a naive parser will render a bogus running zone 6/7.

144449296_fitnessAgeData.json — 142 daily objects. Always present: createTimestamp (local ISO, no zone), asOfDateGmt ("YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.0"), chronologicalAge:int (27, constant), bmi:float, rhr:int (bpm), totalVigorousDays:int, totalVigorousIMs:int (intensity minutes), numOfWeeksForIM:int (6, constant), healthyBmi:float (20.8284, constant), healthyFat:float (14.4875, constant), vo2MaxForHealthyBmiFat:float, biometricVo2Max:float, currentBioAge:float (THIS is the fitness age), healthyAllBioAge:float (18.0, constant floor), healthyBmiFatBioAge:float, weightDataLastEntryDate:"YYYY-MM-DD", rhrLastEntryDate:"YYYY-MM-DD". Present only sometimes: healthyActiveBioAge + vo2MaxForHealthyActive (140/142), healthyRhrBioAge + vo2MaxForHealthyRhr (only 37/142 — they stop appearing after 2026-04-25, so any parser must treat them as optional).

DI-Connect-Aggregator/UDSFile_*.json — THE resting-HR series, and the only place it lives. List of daily objects, 47 fields. HR-relevant: restingHeartRate:int|null (Garmin's published smoothed RHR), currentDayRestingHeartRate:int|null (raw single-day value), restingHeartRateTimestamp:int|null (epoch MILLISECONDS, midnight-local of the calendarDate), minHeartRate/maxHeartRate:int|null (all-day wrist stream extremes), minAvgHeartRate/maxAvgHeartRate:int|null. Plus calendarDate:"YYYY-MM-DD", isVigorousDay:bool, moderateIntensityMinutes/vigorousIntensityMinutes:int, totalSteps, totalDistanceMeters (metres here, NOT centimetres — differs from summarizedActivities), durationInMilliseconds, activeSeconds/highlyActiveSeconds, bodyBattery/allDayStress/respiration/hydration (nested objects), wellnessStartTimeGmt/Local + wellnessEndTimeGmt/Local (epoch ms). Null-heavy: 18 of 161 rows have restingHeartRate null.

DI-Connect-User/user_profile.json — {userName, firstName, lastName, emailAddress, gender:"MALE", birthDate:"1998-11-13"}. No maxHR, no RHR, no weight. user_settings.json is only {preferredLocale:"en", handedness:"RIGHT"} — nothing physiological. The social-profile file has runningTrainingSpeed/cyclingMaxAvgPower etc. but every one is 0.0, i.e. unpopulated.

findings.claim: CONFIRMED — the 86 bpm resting heart rate is a stale, undated, frozen constant inside the heart-rate-zone record, not a measured series. Nothing in the export ever measured 86.
findings.value: restingHeartRateUsed = 86, with restingHrAutoUpdateUsed = false
findings.derivation: DI_CONNECT/DI-Connect-Wellness/144449296_heartRateZones.json, single record, fields restingHeartRateUsed and restingHrAutoUpdateUsed. `grep -rlIi restingHeartRate` over the whole export returns exactly 3 files: this one and the two UDSFile_*.json. The zones file carries no timestamp field of any kind, so the value cannot be aged from within the file. The measured daily series (UDSFile restingHeartRate) never once equals 86 — its 143 non-null values run 54..87 and the only value above 85 is 87 on 2026-03-31. So 86 is a snapshot frozen somewhere in the 2026-03-28..2026-04-03 onboarding window (measured values then: 84, 84, 87, 80) and never refreshed, which restingHrAutoUpdateUsed=false explicitly confirms.

findings.claim: Garmin's own measured resting heart rate is a full daily series and currently sits at 57-60, roughly 27 bpm below the frozen profile constant. It is in the Aggregator UDS files, not in any Wellness biometric file.
findings.value: UDSFile restingHeartRate: 84 on 2026-03-28, falling to 57 on 2026-09-07. n=143 non-null, min 54 (2026-05-27), max 87 (2026-03-31), median 60, mean 62.9. Trailing 30 days (2026-08-09..09-07): 57-60.
findings.derivation: DI_CONNECT/DI-Connect-Aggregator/UDSFile_2026-02-20_2026-05-31.json + UDSFile_2026-05-31_2026-09-08.json, field restingHeartRate, 161 rows concatenated and sorted by calendarDate. Independent corroboration: DI-Connect-Wellness/144449296_fitnessAgeData.json carries its own rhr field over 142 daily rows running 85 -> 58 over the same span; the two series agree to within ~2 bpm on shared dates (2026-03-31 UDS 87 vs fitnessAge 85; 2026-09-07 UDS 57 vs fitnessAge 58), fitnessAge lagging by a day or so. Two independent files, same trajectory.

findings.claim: The athlete's stated true resting rate of ~45 is NOT what Garmin measures either, but it is close to the observed overnight minimum. Garmin's 'resting HR' is a smoothed estimate sitting ~12-15 bpm above the true nightly floor.
findings.value: Observed all-day minimum heart rate (UDSFile minHeartRate) dips to 41-49 routinely; lowest single value 31 on 2026-08-01, next 39 on 2026-05-05, 40 on 2026-08-14, 41 on 2026-04-26 / 2026-07-27 / 2026-08-08. Meanwhile restingHeartRate on those same days reads 58, 61, 57, 71, 59, 60.
findings.derivation: UDSFile_*.json fields minHeartRate vs restingHeartRate, same row. Note 31 bpm on 2026-08-01 is almost certainly a wrist-optical dropout artefact, not physiology — the same row's currentDayRestingHeartRate is 39 against a smoothed 58, a 19 bpm gap seen nowhere else in 161 rows.

findings.claim: The heart-rate zones are built on a max of 196, not the 195 the athlete recalls and not the 201 actually recorded. They are pure percent-of-max — the stored 86 bpm resting rate is arithmetically INERT and does not touch the zone boundaries.
findings.value: maxHeartRateUsed = 196, trainingMethod = HR_MAX. Zone floors 100/118/137/157/176 = 51.0 / 60.2 / 69.9 / 80.1 / 89.8 percent of 196.
findings.derivation: 144449296_heartRateZones.json. Percentages computed as floor/196. Zones 2-5 land on 60/70/80/90 percent to the nearest bpm exactly (0.60*196=117.6->118, 0.70*196=137.2->137, 0.80*196=156.8->157, 0.90*196=176.4->176). The Karvonen/heart-rate-reserve alternative is ruled out: with rhr=86 and max=196 the reserve is 110 and the floors would sit at 12.7/29.1/46.4/64.5/81.8 percent of reserve, which is not any standard scheme. restingHrAutoUpdateUsed=false is consistent with RHR playing no part.

findings.claim: Zone 1's floor of 100 does not fit the pattern the other four floors follow. 50 percent of 196 is 98.
findings.value: zone1Floor = 100 (51.02% of 196), where 50% would be 98 — a 2 bpm mismatch, while zones 2-5 fit their 60/70/80/90 percentages to the bpm.
findings.derivation: 144449296_heartRateZones.json; 0.50*196 = 98.0 vs stored 100. Every other floor rounds cleanly. Either Garmin applies a floor-clamp to zone 1 or this boundary was hand-edited. Low practical stakes (zone 1 is easy aerobic) but it means 'the zones are exactly 50/60/70/80/90 of 196' is not literally true and a parser should not re-derive them.

findings.claim: The zones are therefore wrong at the top: they are built on a max 5 bpm below what the athlete has actually hit, so every zone ceiling and the zone-4/zone-5 boundary are set too low.
findings.derivation: DI_CONNECT/DI-Connect-Fitness/luisdeburnaybastos@gmail.com_1_summarizedActivities.json, field maxHr, sorted descending across all 56 activities; the 201 row is the 2026-06-14 running activity (9.86 km, avgHr 175). Cross-checked against 144449296_heartRateZones.json maxHeartRateUsed=196. The athlete's recollection of 195 appears in no file — 195 is not maxHeartRateUsed (196) and not any activity maximum.

findings.claim: The daily wellness stream and the activity records disagree about the peak heart rate on the same day. The activity file reads higher.
findings.value: 2026-06-14: activity maxHr 201, UDS all-day maxHeartRate 193 (8 bpm gap). 2026-04-11: activity maxHr 199, UDS 196 (3 bpm gap). 2026-06-24: activity 194, UDS 193. 2026-04-25: activity 196, UDS 191.
findings.derivation: summarizedActivities maxHr vs UDSFile_*.json maxHeartRate matched on date. The all-day wellness maximum should by definition be >= any activity maximum inside that day; it is consistently lower. Most likely the UDS stream is the 1-2 minute-sampled wrist optical record while the activity carries the beat-by-beat stream (possibly a chest strap). Whichever explanation, the two sources are not interchangeable and the activity file is the one that saw the peak.

findings.claim: Weight is user-typed, entered twice inside seven seconds on the day the watch was paired, and never touched again in 164 days. There is no body-composition data of any kind.
findings.value: 88.45 kg at 2026-03-28T18:48:28.707, corrected to 85.50 kg at 2026-03-28T18:48:35.449, both sourceType USER_SETTING. weightDataLastEntryDate reads '2026-03-28' on all 142 fitness-age rows including 2026-09-07.
findings.derivation: 144449296_userBioMetrics.json, the two records carrying the nested weight object (weight in grams: 88450.0, 85500.0). Confirmed stale by fitnessAgeData.json weightDataLastEntryDate being constant at 2026-03-28 across the whole 142-row series. A repo-wide grep for bodyFat / bodyComposition / boneMass / muscleMass returns zero files — no smart scale ever connected.

findings.claim: Height was also corrected once on pairing day and is likewise frozen.
findings.value: 175.0 cm then 177.8 cm, both 2026-03-28. 177.8 cm is 5 ft 10 in exactly, so the second value is a unit-conversion entry.
findings.derivation: 144449296_userBioMetrics.json, the two records carrying a bare height field, plus the height repeated on every subsequent threshold record (177.8000030517578 — float32 representation error, read it as 177.8).

findings.claim: The BMI Garmin used for the first week does not reconcile with any height/weight pair stored in the export.
findings.value: bmi = 27.357027387827692 for 2026-03-28 through 2026-04-03, then 27.045971530858164 from 2026-04-04 onward and constant thereafter. The later value is exactly 85.5 kg / 1.778 m^2. The earlier value implies either 86.48 kg at 177.8 cm or 85.5 kg at 176.79 cm — neither pair appears anywhere.
findings.derivation: fitnessAgeData.json bmi field (only 2 distinct values across 142 rows) checked against 144449296_userBioMetrics.json weight/height records. 85.5/(1.778^2) = 85.5/3.161284 = 27.0460. 27.357027*3.161284 = 86.48 kg. Note the BMI changed on 2026-04-04 with no new weight entry (weightDataLastEntryDate stayed 2026-03-28), so this was a server-side recompute, not new data.

findings.claim: Fitness age improved by 4.1 years over the export window and is, mechanically, almost a pure function of resting heart rate.
findings.value: currentBioAge 28.44 on 2026-03-28 -> 24.32 on 2026-09-07, against a chronologicalAge of 27 held constant. Slope: roughly 0.105 years of fitness age per bpm of RHR across the 58-79 range.
findings.derivation: fitnessAgeData.json currentBioAge and rhr, 142 rows. Grouping bioAge by rhr gives a single value per rhr for 20 of the 27 distinct rhr levels: rhr 64->25.02, 65->25.12, 66->25.23, 67->25.33, 68->25.43, 69->25.53, 70->25.64, 71->25.74, 72->25.84, 73->25.95, 75->26.66, 76->26.75, 77->26.84, 78->26.93, 79->27.02 — a clean ~0.10/bpm ladder. bmi is frozen at 27.046 and chronologicalAge at 27, so RHR is the only continuously moving input.

findings.claim: The second, smaller driver of fitness age is the count of vigorous days in the trailing 6-week window, which acts as a step adjustment rather than a continuous term.
findings.value: At 18 vigorous days a bonus of ~0.7 years applies: rhr 59 + 18 days -> 23.73 (2026-08-04) vs rhr 59 + 17 days -> 24.44; rhr 58 + 18 days -> 23.60 (2026-08-22) vs rhr 58 + 17 days -> 24.32. Below 12 vigorous days a penalty applies: rhr 59 + 11 days -> 25.10 (2026-05-31) vs rhr 59 + 12 days -> 24.44 (2026-05-30).
findings.derivation: fitnessAgeData.json, rows compared pairwise holding rhr fixed and varying totalVigorousDays. numOfWeeksForIM is constant at 6, so 'vigorous days' is counted over a 6-week trailing window. The exposed attribution fields are healthyBmiFatBioAge (what the fitness age would be at a healthy BMI/fat), healthyRhrBioAge (only populated on 37 of 142 rows, all before 2026-04-26), healthyActiveBioAge, and healthyAllBioAge (constant 18.0 — the floor, i.e. best achievable).

findings.claim: Running power zones are built on an auto-detected running FTP of 454 W that has been drifting downward, and the running sport uses only 5 of the 7 zone slots.
findings.derivation: 144449296_powerZones.json for the zone floors (percentages = floor/454). FTP history from 144449296_userBioMetrics.json, records with sportId=1, ordered by calendarDate. ftpAutoDetected is true on every threshold record, so none of this was entered by the athlete.

findings.claim: The 300 W treadmill run is NOT implausible for the athlete — it is implausible for the zone model. Garmin running power on a treadmill reads roughly 110 W (27 percent) below outdoor power at the same pace, which drops a genuinely moderate effort into zone 1.
findings.value: 2026-09-05 treadmill_running, 10.00 km, 4.92 min/km, avgPower 300 W, avgHr 141, maxHr 181. Outdoor runs at 4.86-4.99 min/km record 411-429 W: 2026-06-14 4.96 min/km 416 W, 2026-06-24 4.92 min/km 411 W, 2026-06-28 4.98 min/km 411 W, 2026-08-16 4.86 min/km 417 W, 2026-08-01 4.99 min/km 399 W. Median outdoor running power across 52 activities is 403.5 W. The other treadmill run (2026-08-15, 7.44 min/km) reads 257 W against outdoor 271-277 W at the same pace.
findings.derivation: summarizedActivities: pace computed as (duration_ms/1000/60)/(distance_cm/100/1000), power read from avgPower. 300 W against powerZones RUNNING floors puts the treadmill run in zone 1 (297-362 W); the identically-paced outdoor runs land in zone 3 (409-454 W). Sanity check on the pace derivation: 1000000 cm / 2953512 ms = 3.3858 m/s and the stored avgSpeed for that row is 0.3386, ratio 9.9994 — confirming the x10 speed scaling before any pace was computed.

findings.claim: The two 'latest biometrics' files disagree on functionalThresholdPower because neither labels the sport, and the athlete has never once cycled.
findings.value: bioMetrics_latest.json functionalThresholdPower = 237 (the CYCLING value). userBioMetricProfileData.json functionalThresholdPower = 454 (the RUNNING value). Stored FTPs also include CROSS_COUNTRY_SKIING 142 W.
findings.derivation: The three sport-tagged values in 144449296_powerZones.json (RUNNING 454, CYCLING 237, XC 142) disambiguate the two unlabelled scalars. Activity census from summarizedActivities: Counter({'running': 52, 'treadmill_running': 2, 'hiking': 2}) — zero cycling, zero skiing, so the 237 W and 142 W FTPs and their full 7-zone ladders are Garmin defaults with no observation behind them.

findings.claim: Lactate threshold is auto-detected, well-populated, and internally consistent — the one biometric here that is genuinely current.
findings.derivation: 144449296_userBioMetrics.json threshold records (those carrying lactateThresholdSpeed), with thresholdHeartRateAutoDetected=true on every one. Speed converted by the verified x10 factor then 1000/v to seconds per km: 1000/3.8333 = 260.9 s = 4:20.9. Confirmed as the current value by 144449296_bioMetrics_latest.json (0.38333226, 177) and userBioMetricProfileData.json (177.0). LTHR 177 sits at 90.3 percent of the 196 max the zones use and 88.1 percent of the observed 201 — both physiologically sane, which is a mild independent vote for the max being real.

findings.claim: VO2max is current and rising; it is the best-maintained metric in the domain.
findings.derivation: 144449296_userBioMetrics.json vo2MaxRunning across 60 records; agrees with userBioMetricProfileData.json vo2Max 53.0 and with DI-Connect-Metrics/MetricsMaxMetData_20260706_20261014_144449296.json (2026-09-02, vo2MaxValue 53.0, maxMet 15.12, calibratedData 1). Note fitnessAgeData carries a SEPARATE and much lower biometricVo2Max (40.15 -> 47.07) — that is a modelled figure derived from BMI/RHR/activity for the fitness-age calculation, NOT the measured running VO2max. Do not conflate them.

findings.claim: Sleep data in this export is effectively empty and cannot support any recovery modelling.
findings.value: 162 sleep records across 3 files; 160 of them are the literal object {"retro": false} with no date and no payload. Only 2 records (2026-06-25 and 2026-07-18) carry sleep stages, scores and respiration. healthStatusData likewise has only those same 2 dates, both with status ONBOARDING and zeroed baselines.
findings.derivation: DI_CONNECT/DI-Connect-Wellness/*sleepData.json — counted records containing a calendarDate key: file 2025-04-27_2025-08-05 has 1 record / 0 dated; 2026-02-21_2026-06-01 has 64 records / 0 dated; 2026-06-01_2026-09-09 has 97 records / 2 dated. 2026-06-25_2026-07-18_144449296_healthStatusData.json has 2 rows.

unitTraps: weight is GRAMS (85500.0 = 85.5 kg), not kilograms and not the centigrams you might expect by analogy with distance-in-centimetres. Verified by recomputing BMI: 85.5/(1.778^2) = 27.046 matches the stored bmi to 5 significant figures.
height is CENTIMETRES as a float32 round-trip: 177.8000030517578 means 177.8 cm. Do not print it raw.

avgSpeed / maxSpeed / lactateThresholdSpeed must be MULTIPLIED BY 10 to get m/s. The task brief says avgSpeed is 'numerically equal to m/s (0.3386 means 3.386 m/s)' — that phrasing is right about the decoded value but the field is NOT in m/s, and it is not cm/ms either (cm/ms would be 10 m/s). I verified the factor on 6 activities: (distance_cm/100)/(duration_ms/1000) divided by avgSpeed gave 9.9983, 9.9991, 9.9993, 9.9994, 9.9997, 10.0015. Consequence for this domain: lactateThresholdSpeed 0.38333226 is 3.8333 m/s (4:21/km), not 0.383 m/s (43 min/km).

restingHeartRateTimestamp in the UDS files is epoch MILLISECONDS and lands on local midnight of that row's calendarDate — it is not the time of day the reading was taken. Do not use it as a measurement instant.

firstbeatRunningLtTimestamp in userBioMetrics is a Garmin/FIT epoch (seconds since 1989-12-31 00:00:00 UTC), NOT Unix seconds. 1155133851 decodes to 2026-08-08, matching its own calendarDate; read as Unix it would land in 2006.

totalDistanceMeters in the UDS aggregator files is METRES, while distance in summarizedActivities is CENTIMETRES. Same export, same concept, two different units, two different field names. Never cross-compare without converting.

In powerZones.json a 0.0 zone floor means the zone is unused for that sport, not a zone starting at 0 W. RUNNING has zone6Floor=zone7Floor=0.0 (5 zones); CYCLING and XC have zone1Floor=0.0 (zones effectively 2-7).

functionalThresholdPower appears unlabelled by sport in BOTH bioMetrics_latest.json (237 = cycling) and userBioMetricProfileData.json (454 = running). Only powerZones.json carries the sport tag. Reading either scalar without cross-referencing gives a 2x error.

lactateThresholdHearRate in userBioMetrics.json is misspelled (no T in 'Heart'). The same concept is lactateThresholdHeartRate in bioMetrics_latest.json and userBioMetricProfileData.json, and lactateThresholdHeartRateUsed in heartRateZones.json. Four spellings, one metric.

fitnessAgeData.biometricVo2Max (40-47) is a MODELLED value used to compute fitness age; userBioMetrics.vo2MaxRunning (48-53) is the measured running VO2max. Both are float, both named like VO2max, ~6 points apart. Conflating them understates fitness by a full training year.
dataQualityIssues: The 86 bpm resting heart rate in heartRateZones.json is a frozen onboarding-era constant with restingHrAutoUpdateUsed=false and no timestamp. Current measured value is 57-60. Error: +28 bpm.

Max heart rate used for zones (196) is 5 bpm below the highest recorded activity value (201 on 2026-06-14) and 3 bpm below the second (199 on 2026-04-11). Every zone boundary above zone 1 is therefore set low.
zone1Floor of 100 is 51.0% of 196 where the other four floors sit on clean 60/70/80/90 percentages. 50% of 196 would be 98. Unexplained 2 bpm.

Weight (85.5 kg) and height (177.8 cm) were entered once on 2026-03-28 and never updated in 164 days. weightDataLastEntryDate is still '2026-03-28' on the 2026-09-07 row. A marathon build normally moves weight several kg.
No body composition data whatsoever — repo-wide grep for bodyFat/bodyComposition/boneMass/muscleMass returns zero files. No smart scale has ever connected.

BMI for 2026-03-28..2026-04-03 (27.357) reconciles with no stored height/weight pair; it implies ~86.5 kg at 177.8 cm, a weight never recorded. It silently changed to the correct 27.046 on 2026-04-04 with no new weight entry.
Sleep data is 160 empty {"retro": false} stubs out of 162 records. Only 2026-06-25 and 2026-07-18 have content. Any sleep-based recovery input is unavailable.
healthStatusData has 2 rows, both with status ONBOARDING and baselineUpperLimit/baselineLowerLimit of 0.0 — the HRV baseline never established.

The UDS daily maxHeartRate is systematically LOWER than the activity-file maxHr on the same day (8 bpm gap on 2026-06-14), which is logically impossible if both describe the same day. The all-day wellness stream is under-sampling peaks.
restingHeartRate is null on 18 of 161 UDS days, clustered around 2026-04-01/02/06/07/08 and 2026-05-03/08/15/25 — watch not worn overnight. A backfill must not forward-fill these silently.

currentDayRestingHeartRate (raw) is wildly noisier than restingHeartRate (smoothed) and occasionally absurd: 39 on 2026-08-01 against a smoothed 58, and 97 on 2026-04-12 against a smoothed 81. Use the smoothed field.
No biometric data exists before 2026-03-28. Whatever the athlete's history is, this export does not contain it — the 'full history' is 164 days.

Cycling FTP 237 W and cross-country-skiing FTP 142 W are stored with full 7-zone ladders despite zero cycling and zero skiing activities in the entire export. They are defaults, and bioMetrics_latest.json surfaces the cycling one as the headline FTP.

healthyRhrBioAge and vo2MaxForHealthyRhr are present on only 37 of 142 fitness-age rows and stop entirely after 2026-04-25 — a parser assuming a fixed schema will crash or silently drop the RHR attribution.
surprises: The brief warns that the export is treacherous but frames the ~42-day API window as the limitation this export lifts. It does not: the biometric domain starts 2026-03-28, 164 days before the export date. There is no long history to backfill from here — this is 5.4 months, not years. If rocket's CTL model wants a 42-day EWMA warm-up, the first ~6 weeks of any backfill (2026-03-28 to mid-May) are cold-start and should be treated as unreliable, leaving roughly 4 months of trustworthy load history.

The athlete's premise that 86 corrupts heart-rate-reserve calculations is right in principle but the 86 is NOT currently corrupting his Garmin zones. trainingMethod is HR_MAX and restingHrAutoUpdateUsed is false — the zones are pure percent-of-max and never touch RHR. The 86 is a landmine waiting for anything (rocket included) that reads the profile and applies Karvonen. The zones are wrong for a different reason: the max is 196, not 201.

The athlete recalls Garmin 'recently detecting a new max of 195'. 195 appears nowhere in the export — not as maxHeartRateUsed (196), not as any activity maxHr, not as any UDS daily maximum. Either the detection post-dates the export, or the recollection is off by one.

The 300 W treadmill run is not the anomaly it looks like. Garmin running power on a treadmill runs ~27% below outdoor power at identical pace (300 W vs 411-429 W at 4.9-5.0 min/km, and 257 W vs 271-277 W at 7.4 min/km on the second treadmill run). The power number is fine as a treadmill number; what is broken is comparing it to outdoor-derived zones.

Fitness age is almost entirely a resting-heart-rate readout dressed up as a composite. With BMI frozen at 27.046 and chronological age constant, RHR moves fitness age on a clean ~0.10 years-per-bpm ladder, with only a step bonus at >=18 vigorous days and a step penalty below 12. It carries essentially no independent information beyond the RHR series rocket already has.

The 'latest biometrics' file (bioMetrics_latest.json) reports the CYCLING FTP as its headline functionalThresholdPower for an athlete who has never cycled. It is the most-obviously-named file in the domain and it is the most misleading one.

Resting HR did not fall monotonically. It bottomed at 54-55 in late May 2026 and then ROSE back to 64-65 through mid-June before settling at 57-60. The May trough coincides with the 42.67 km run on 2026-05-10; the June rise coincides with the 2026-06-14 effort that produced the 201 max. That is a plausible fatigue signature and rocket's TSB model should be able to reproduce it as a sanity check on the backfill.
mined.rocketRelevance:
BACKFILL — take these as-is: (1) The daily resting-HR series from DI-Connect-Aggregator/UDSFile_*.json, field restingHeartRate, 143 non-null days 2026-03-28..2026-09-07. This is the only RHR series in the export and it is the authoritative one. Use restingHeartRate (smoothed), NOT currentDayRestingHeartRate (noisy, produces 39 and 97 outliers). Do not forward-fill the 18 null days. (2) The VO2max series from userBioMetrics.json vo2MaxRunning, 60 points, 48->53 — useful as an independent fitness trend to validate CTL against. (3) Lactate threshold: LTHR 177 bpm, LT pace 4:21/km as of 2026-08-08, auto-detected and current. This is the single most useful number here for pacing the 2026-09-12 half and the 2026-10-24 marathon, and it is far better grounded than the zones. 177 bpm is 88% of the observed 201 max. (4) The activity-file maxHr series as the max-HR oracle, not the UDS daily maxHeartRate.

IGNORE — do not read into rocket at all: (1) heartRateZones.json restingHeartRateUsed=86. It is stale by 28 bpm. If rocket computes heart-rate reserve, hardcode nothing from this file. (2) bioMetrics_latest.json functionalThresholdPower=237 — that is a cycling default for a non-cyclist. (3) The cycling and XC-ski power zones entirely. (4) Sleep data and healthStatusData — 2 usable days out of 162 records; no recovery signal exists. (5) fitnessAgeData.biometricVo2Max — a modelled artefact, not a measurement; use vo2MaxRunning instead. (6) currentBioAge/fitness age as an input — it is a near-linear restatement of RHR, so feeding it alongside RHR double-counts the same signal.

CROSS-CHECK — use, but against something else: (1) Running power. The 454 W FTP and its 297/362/409/454/523 W zones are outdoor-calibrated. Any treadmill activity must be excluded from power-zone classification or corrected upward by ~27%, or rocket will score a 4:55/km treadmill 10 km as zone-1 recovery. Two of 56 activities are treadmill; the 2026-09-05 one is the most recent run in the export, four days before race week. (2) The 5-week 60/80/100/80/60 km build against the RHR series: RHR rose from 55 to 65 in the two weeks after the 42.67 km run on 2026-05-10, which is a usable empirical prior for what this athlete's overreaching looks like. (3) The single-session spike guardrail (110% of longest run in trailing 30 days) is directly computable from summarizedActivities distance/100/1000, and the 2026-05-10 42.67 km run against a prior 30-day longest of 30.11 km (2026-04-12) is a 142% spike — a historical violation rocket's guardrail should flag when it backfills, confirming the rule fires.

ASK THE ATHLETE TO FIX IN GARMIN BEFORE RELYING ON IT: (1) Resting heart rate — Garmin's zone profile holds 86; turn on auto-update or set it to the measured 57-60. Note his stated 45 is his overnight floor, not Garmin's resting definition, and setting 45 manually would over-correct in the other direction. Recommend enabling auto-update rather than typing a number. (2) Max heart rate — set to 201, or at minimum re-run Garmin's auto-detect. 196 costs him 4-5 bpm on every zone ceiling, which for the 2026-09-12 half means his "HR under 170 at 10 km" decision point sits at 86.7% of the profile max but 84.6% of his real one; the raw 170 bpm trigger is unaffected, but any %-based translation is. (3) Weight — 85.5 kg is 164 days stale and predates the entire build. Every calorie, power-to-weight and BMI figure downstream inherits the error. (4) Running FTP is auto-detected and has drifted 470->390->461->454; it does not need manual correction, but rocket should re-read it rather than caching it.
