domains.title: Daily summaries — steps, stress, body battery, resting HR

mined.domain: Daily wellness summaries (UDS) — steps, resting HR, stress, body battery, intensity minutes, calories, floors — plus hydration logs
mined.recordCounts: UDS: 161 records, one per calendar date, 2026-03-28 through 2026-09-07 inclusive. Zero duplicate dates. Calendar span is 164 days, so 3 dates are absent (2026-08-29, 08-30, 08-31). The two filenames LIE about their coverage: `UDSFile_2026-02-20_2026-05-31.json` holds 64 records starting 2026-03-28 (nothing from 2026-02-20 to 03-27 exists); `UDSFile_2026-05-31_2026-09-08.json` holds 97 records ending 2026-09-07 (no record for 09-08, the export date). Hydration: 56 records over 53 distinct dates, 2026-03-28 to 2026-09-05.
mined.schemaNotes:
UDS file = JSON array of flat-ish objects, one per calendar day, with four nested sub-objects. Populated-fraction is out of 161 records.

TOP LEVEL (identity / window):
- userProfilePK int 144449296 (100%); uuid str hex32 (100%); version int 1..86280000 (100%, meaningless); source int always 0.
- calendarDate str "YYYY-MM-DD" (100%) — THE join key. Local calendar day.
- durationInMilliseconds int (100%) — length of the day's measurement window in ms. NOT always 86400000: observed 11.00h, 16.00h, 19.40h, 23.02h, 23.30h, 24.00h, 25.00h, 32.00h. Use it to weight partial days.
- wellnessStartTimeGmt / wellnessEndTimeGmt / wellnessStartTimeLocal / wellnessEndTimeLocal str "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.0" (100%) — ISO strings, NOT epoch ms (unlike summarizedActivities.json). Local variants are already shifted; read as naive local.

CALORIES (kcal, floats, 100% populated):
- totalKilocalories == bmrKilocalories + activeKilocalories, verified exactly on 161/161 records.
- wellnessKilocalories == wellnessTotalKilocalories == totalKilocalories on 161/161 (pure duplicates — parse one).
- wellnessActiveKilocalories == activeKilocalories. restingCaloriesFromActivity float 10..367 (33% only).
- Range: total 1042..5972; bmr 1024..2980; active 0..3737.

STEPS / DISTANCE:
- totalSteps int 136..46647 (145/161 = 90.1%). Null on watch-off days.
- totalDistanceMeters int 110..50597 (90.1%) — METRES, not centimetres. Verified two ways: (a) implied stride totalDistanceMeters/totalSteps has median 0.846 m/step, range 0.756..1.290, i.e. human; (b) on 2026-05-10 the activity file records a 42.70 km run and UDS totalDistanceMeters is 50597 = 50.6 km, which is the run plus daily walking. Centimetres would give 506 m for a marathon day.
- wellnessDistanceMeters == totalDistanceMeters on 161/161 (duplicate).
- dailyStepGoal int 6590..16300 (adaptive goal, 100%).

ACTIVITY TIME:
- highlyActiveSeconds int 0..14572 (100%), activeSeconds int 0..12077 (100%) — SECONDS.
- moderateIntensityMinutes int 0..111, vigorousIntensityMinutes int 0..235 (both 100%) — MINUTES. Weekly goal metric is mod + 2*vig against userIntensityMinutesGoal (150, constant).
- isVigorousDay bool (57/161 true). NOT equal to vigorousIntensityMinutes>0 — mismatches on 2026-04-20, 04-27, 04-28, 04-30, 05-06, 05-14, 05-17, 05-20, 05-23, 05-24 and more. Do not derive it; do not trust it.

FLOORS:
- floorsAscendedInMeters float 0.0..533.4, floorsDescendedInMeters float 0.0..551.67 (100%) — genuine METRES of ascent, NOT floor counts and NOT quantised: only 31 of 144 non-zero values are exact multiples of 3.048 (one Garmin "floor"). e.g. 201.876 m = 66.232 floors.
- userFloorsAscendedGoal int constant 10.

HEART RATE (the important part — two different fields, different semantics):
- minHeartRate int 31..83 (92.5%), maxHeartRate int 70..196 (92.5%) — day extremes.
- minAvgHeartRate int 32..84, maxAvgHeartRate int 70..195 (92.5%) — smoothed extremes; near-duplicates of the above.
- currentDayRestingHeartRate int 39..97 (143/161 = 88.8%) — the RAW measured resting HR for that day.
- restingHeartRate int 54..87 (88.8%) — a SMOOTHED value, not that day's measurement. It differs from currentDayRestingHeartRate on 136 of 143 days. Fitting trailing means of currentDayRestingHeartRate: MAE 2.15 bpm at window 3, 1.11 at window 5, 0.63 at window 7, 1.61 at window 14. It is a 7-day trailing mean.
- restingHeartRateTimestamp int epoch MILLISECONDS, always midnight UTC of calendarDate (1774742400000 = 2026-03-29T00:00:00Z).

NESTED allDayStress (100% present, always 3 aggregators):
- allDayStress.aggregatorList[] with type in {TOTAL, AWAKE, ASLEEP}. TOTAL and AWAKE are byte-identical in this export — parse TOTAL only. ASLEEP has averageStressLevel = -2 on 159/161 days (no data); only 2 days carry real sleep stress (values 7 and 4). Sleep stress is effectively absent from UDS.
- Per aggregator: averageStressLevel int 0..100 (SENTINELS: -1 = no data on 13 days, -2 = not measured on 1 day — must be nulled, never averaged); averageStressLevelIntensity (duplicate of averageStressLevel); maxStressLevel int; stressIntensityCount, stressOffWristCount, stressTooActiveCount, totalStressCount ints — these are counts of 1-MINUTE samples (verified: totalDuration == totalStressCount * 60 on 161/161).
- Durations in SECONDS: stressDuration, activityDuration, uncategorizedDuration, totalDuration, lowDuration, mediumDuration, highDuration. Identity stressDuration == lowDuration + mediumDuration + highDuration holds on 144/144 records where stressDuration exists; the other 17 records omit the duration keys entirely (see gaps).
- totalDuration == stressDuration + activityDuration + uncategorizedDuration. stressOffWristCount and stressTooActiveCount are OUTSIDE totalDuration — use stressOffWristCount (minutes) as the watch-off detector: 1436 on 2026-08-28 = 23.9 h off wrist.

NESTED bodyBattery (153/161 have the object, 151/161 have the stat list):
- bodyBattery.chargedValue int 0..77, drainedValue int 0..81 — net charge/drain within the recorded window. These do NOT reconcile with HIGHEST−LOWEST because the overnight charge straddles midnight. Do not derive one from the other.
- bodyBattery.bodyBatteryVersion float 3.0; calendarDate; userProfilePK.
- bodyBattery.bodyBatteryStatList[] of {bodyBatteryStatType, statsValue int 0..100, bodyBatteryStatus, statTimestamp "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.0" local}.
  - bodyBatteryStatType counts: HIGHEST 151, LOWEST 151, MOSTRECENT 151, STARTOFDAY 151, ENDOFDAY 18, SLEEPSTART 2, SLEEPEND 2, DURINGSLEEP 2. Only HIGHEST/LOWEST/MOSTRECENT/STARTOFDAY are reliably present.
  - bodyBatteryStatus in {MEASURED 304, RESET 282, MODELED 42}. RESET dominates the HIGHEST/STARTOFDAY rows — it marks the post-sleep reset point, which is exactly the morning readiness number you want. MODELED means Garmin filled it in; treat as lower confidence.
- Distribution: HIGHEST n=151 min 29 max 100 mean 80.1 median 89; LOWEST n=151 min 9 max 98 mean 43.1 median 42.

NESTED bodyBatteryFeedback (44% populated, 62-71/161): coaching-copy IDs only — feedbackLongType / feedbackShortType ints (300..588), bodyBatteryLevel int 2..4, eventTimestampGmt as a 6-element array, deviceId 3613943939. No decoded strings. Useless to rocket; skip entirely.

NESTED respiration (147/161 = 91.3%): avgWakingRespirationValue float 10..20, highestRespirationValue 10..27, lowestRespirationValue 5..20, latestRespirationValue 8..22 — BREATHS PER MINUTE. latestRespirationTimeGMT ISO string. algorithmVersion 200.

NESTED hydration (53/161 = 32.9%): valueInML float — ALWAYS 0.0, on every one of the 53 records. goalInML constant 2839.056; sweatLossInML float 76..3928 (auto-estimated from activities); adjustedGoalInML = goalInML + sweatLossInML; activityIntakeInML always 0.0; capped bool; lastEntryTimestampLocal ISO string.

OTHER:
- averageMonitoringEnvironmentAltitude float −57.0..584.0 — barometric METRES, useful as a crude travel/location detector.
- includesWellnessData / includesActivityData / includesCalorieConsumedData / includesSingleMeasurement / includesContinuousMeasurement / includesAllDayPulseOx / includesSleepPulseOx bools (100%). Pulse-ox flags are false throughout — no SpO2 data anywhere.
- dailyTotalFromEpochData bool, present on only 5/161 records.

HYDRATION LOG FILE = JSON array, keys: userProfilePK, calendarDate, persistedTimestampGMT, timestampLocal (both ISO strings), hydrationSource, valueInML, activityId (int, joins to summarizedActivities), capped, estimatedSweatLossInML float, duration float SECONDS (5293.891 = 88.2 min), uuid {uuid: str}.

findings.claim: The 86 bpm resting heart rate is a stale onboarding constant, not a measurement. It lives in heartRateZones.json, not in any daily record, and auto-update is explicitly switched off.
findings.value: restingHeartRateUsed = 86, restingHrAutoUpdateUsed = false. Measured RHR across the whole export: median 60, mean 62.9, min 54, max 87 (smoothed field); raw daily field median 62, mean 62.4, min 39, max 97.
findings.derivation: DI_CONNECT/DI-Connect-Wellness/144449296_heartRateZones.json fields restingHeartRateUsed and restingHrAutoUpdateUsed. Compared against restingHeartRate and currentDayRestingHeartRate across all 161 UDS records (143 non-null). 86 sits inside the 84-87 band the athlete recorded on 2026-03-28/29/31 — the first three days of the export — and is never approached again after 2026-04-12. The zone config was frozen at watch onboarding.

findings.claim: Measured resting heart rate by month (SMOOTHED field restingHeartRate, which is what Garmin Connect displays).
findings.derivation: Grouped restingHeartRate by calendarDate[:7] across both UDSFiles; Python statistics.mean/median. Only 143 of 161 days carry the field. The March mean is built on 3 days only and reflects an untrained-and-newly-worn-watch baseline; treat 2026-05 onward as the real series.

findings.claim: restingHeartRate and currentDayRestingHeartRate are DIFFERENT metrics and rocket must not treat them as interchangeable. restingHeartRate is a 7-day trailing mean; currentDayRestingHeartRate is the raw daily reading.
findings.value: They disagree on 136 of 143 days. Fitting trailing means of currentDayRestingHeartRate against restingHeartRate: MAE 2.15 bpm (3-day), 1.11 (5-day), 0.63 (7-day), 1.61 (14-day). Raw stdev 7.8 bpm vs smoothed stdev 6.2 bpm.
findings.derivation: Both UDSFiles; for each date computed the trailing-window mean of currentDayRestingHeartRate and the absolute error against restingHeartRate on the same date. Window 7 is the clear minimum. Worst single-day divergence: 2026-08-01, raw 39 vs smoothed 58 (19 bpm).

findings.claim: Raw resting HR is physically impossible on 7 days — it falls BELOW the same day's recorded minimum heart rate.
findings.derivation: Both UDSFiles; filtered records where currentDayRestingHeartRate < minHeartRate. The pattern (all long-run days, minHR unusually high at 63-76) says the watch was off overnight so minHeartRate only covers the awake window, while the RHR figure was carried over or modelled. Null the raw RHR on days where currentDayRestingHeartRate < minHeartRate.

findings.claim: Full daily series, one record per line, pipe-delimited. Fields: MM-DD | totalSteps | currentDayRestingHeartRate(raw) | restingHeartRate(7d smoothed) | averageStressLevel | bodyBatteryHIGHEST | bodyBatteryLOWEST | moderateIntensityMinutes | vigorousIntensityMinutes | totalKilocalories | floorsAscendedInMeters(rounded). Empty field = null or sentinel. All dates are 2026.
findings.derivation: Both UDSFiles, sorted by calendarDate. Steps = totalSteps; raw RHR = currentDayRestingHeartRate; smoothed RHR = restingHeartRate; stress = allDayStress.aggregatorList[type=TOTAL].averageStressLevel with -1/-2 sentinels blanked; body battery from bodyBattery.bodyBatteryStatList entries HIGHEST and LOWEST; intensity minutes and totalKilocalories verbatim; floors = round(floorsAscendedInMeters). Every day where totalKilocalories == 2235 and steps is blank is a fully watch-off day: 2235 is the pure BMR floor with activeKilocalories 0.

findings.claim: Body battery is a same-day cost signal, not a next-day readiness signal. It records that a hard session happened; it does not predict how the athlete will feel tomorrow.
findings.value: Correlation of daily activity training load with same-day body battery LOWEST = -0.415 (n=53). Correlation with NEXT-day body battery HIGHEST = +0.091 (n=48). Correlation with next-day raw resting HR = +0.137 (n=44).
findings.derivation: Summed activityTrainingLoad per local day from summarizedActivities.json (startTimeLocal / 1000 -> date), joined to UDS by calendarDate, Pearson correlation computed in Python. Concretely, after the three biggest sessions: 2026-05-10 (42.7 km, load 462) body battery next morning reached 88; 2026-08-02 (29.7 km, load 491) reached 87; 2026-08-09 (31.5 km, load 340) reached 81 — all within one point of the 80.1 all-time mean. The overnight recharge fully masks the session.

findings.claim: The useful hard-session marker is the same-day body-battery trough, and it fires reliably.
findings.value: On the 15 highest-load days the same-day LOWEST value was 10, 36, 28, 10, 44, 22, 20, 52, 38, 30, 19, 29, 10, 22, 9 — median 22 against an all-days median of 42. Four of the six all-time lowest troughs (9, 10, 10, 10) are long-run Sundays: 2026-08-09, 2026-04-26, 2026-07-26, 2026-03-28.
findings.derivation: bodyBattery.bodyBatteryStatList[type=LOWEST].statsValue on the 15 days with the largest summed activityTrainingLoad, versus the distribution over all 151 days that carry the field (min 9, max 98, mean 43.1, median 42).

findings.claim: Stress in the days before a hard session carries no predictive signal either — the pre-session values sit squarely in the middle of the distribution.
findings.value: Day-before averageStressLevel across the 15 top-load sessions: 13, 41, 29, no-data, 31, 14, 25, no-data, 38, 26, 12, 23, 29, 28 — mean 25.7 against an all-days mean around 26. Day-after values: 76, 17, 24, 12, 20, 25, no-data, 17, 26, 32, 35, 29, 57, 24.
findings.derivation: allDayStress.aggregatorList[type=TOTAL].averageStressLevel on D-1 and D+1 for the 15 highest activityTrainingLoad days. The one striking pre-session number, 2026-05-04 at 79, precedes a load-290 session but is itself a no-data day artefact adjacent to a gap.

findings.claim: UDS coverage gaps do NOT align with the training gaps — the two are independent, so UDS cannot be used to infer whether training happened.
findings.value: Only 3 dates are entirely absent (2026-08-29, 08-30, 08-31). A further 15 dates have a record but no wellness data at all (watch off): 2026-03-30, 04-01, 04-02, 04-06, 04-07, 04-08, 04-24, 05-03, 05-08, 05-15, 05-21, 05-25, 06-02, 06-17, 08-28. Meanwhile the longest TRAINING gap — 23 days with no activity, 2026-05-11 to 2026-06-02 — has near-complete UDS coverage (only 05-15, 05-21, 05-25 missing wellness).
findings.derivation: Enumerated every date from 2026-03-28 to 2026-09-07 against the UDS date set; separately flagged records where totalSteps is null. Training gaps computed from distinct activity days in summarizedActivities.json: gaps over 3 days are 05-10->06-03 (23 days), 08-22->09-02 (10 days), 07-20->07-26 and 07-26->08-01 (5 days each), 06-14->06-19 and 07-14->07-19 (4 days each).

findings.claim: UDS and the activity file agree perfectly on which days contained hard efforts. No orphan sessions in either direction.
findings.value: Zero UDS days with vigorousIntensityMinutes >= 25 that lack an activity record. Zero activity days that lack a UDS record.
findings.derivation: Set difference between the 53 distinct activity days from summarizedActivities.json and the 161 UDS calendarDates, both ways, plus a filter on UDS vigorousIntensityMinutes. This makes UDS a usable completeness oracle for the activity backfill.

findings.claim: Last 14 days (2026-08-25 to 2026-09-08), day by day. Format: date | run km | training load | steps | raw RHR | smoothed RHR | bbHIGH | bbLOW | avg stress | vigorous intensity min.
findings.value: 08-25 Tue | 0.0 | 0 | 12453 | 63 | 60 | 78 | 24 | 36 | 1 -- first full rest day after the 08-22 16 km session. 08-26 Wed | 0.0 | 0 | 8095 | 58 | 59 | 85 | 45 | 22 | 0. 08-27 Thu | 0.0 | 0 | 6586 | 58 | 60 | 94 | 65 | 21 | 0 -- body battery peak 94, trough 65, the cleanest recovery day of the fortnight. 08-28 Fri | 0.0 | 0 | no steps | null | null | 38 | 37 | 29 | 0 -- watch off: stressOffWristCount 1436 minutes = 23.9 h, calories flat at BMR 2235. 08-29 Sat, 08-30 Sun, 08-31 Mon | NO UDS RECORD AT ALL. 09-01 Tue | 0.0 | 0 | 13656 | 72 | 60 | 91 | 27 | 47 | 12 -- raw RHR spikes to 72, the highest since 2026-08-03; stress 47 and 236 m of ascent on foot; consistent with a travel day. 09-02 Wed | 4.8 | 127 | 13412 | 56 | 60 | 71 | 28 | 22 | 37 -- the Soller (Mallorca) run, 25.5 min, avg HR 156, max HR 191; the calendar day is 25 h long, i.e. a UTC+2 -> UTC+1 return. 09-03 Thu | 0.0 | 0 | 7801 | 56 | 60 | 89 | 42 | 21 | 0. 09-04 Fri | 0.0 | 0 | 10219 | 52 | 58 | 84 | 41 | 17 | 2. 09-05 Sat | 16.1 | 144 | 32880 | 55 | 58 | 80 | 23 | 18 | 53 -- 10.0 km treadmill (49.2 min, avg HR 141, max 181) plus 6.09 km hiking (125 min, avg HR 106); 111 moderate intensity minutes, the highest single-day moderate figure in the whole export. 09-06 Sun | 0.0 | 0 | 7750 | 56 | 59 | 56 | 40 | 35 | 9 -- body battery HIGHEST only 56, the second-lowest peak in the fortnight; 1206 minutes off wrist, so partial coverage. 09-07 Mon | 0.0 | 0 | 8052 | 50 | 57 | 91 | 72 | 14 | 0 -- 19.4 h day. 09-08 Tue | NO UDS RECORD (export cut).
findings.derivation: UDSFile_2026-05-31_2026-09-08.json filtered to calendarDate >= 2026-08-25, joined to per-day sums from summarizedActivities.json. Run distances are distance/100000 (centimetres to km); loads are activityTrainingLoad; body battery from the HIGHEST/LOWEST stat entries; off-wrist from allDayStress TOTAL stressOffWristCount, which counts 1-minute samples.

findings.claim: Current recovery state 4 days out from the Battersea Half: strongly recovered, and every independent daily metric agrees.
findings.value: 2026-09-07 raw resting HR 50 bpm — the lowest single-day value since 2026-08-01 and 7-9 bpm below the athlete's own summer baseline. Smoothed RHR 57, equal to the lowest value ever recorded in the export (also 57 on 2026-08-11, 08-12, 08-13, 08-14). 2026-09-07 body battery LOWEST 72 — joint 4th-highest trough of all 151 measured days (all-days median 42), meaning the battery never dropped below 72 all day. Body battery HIGHEST 91 versus an all-days median of 89. Average stress 14, versus an all-days mean near 26. Last 14 days raw RHR mean 57.6 (n=10) against 59.1 for the preceding 30 days (n=31).
findings.derivation: UDSFile_2026-05-31_2026-09-08.json, records for 2026-09-01 to 09-07, compared against the full 161-record distributions. Cross-checked independently against DI-Connect-Metrics/TrainingReadinessDTO_20260706_20261014_144449296.json, which for 2026-09-07 gives score 79, level HIGH, recoveryTime 1 minute, acuteLoad 228 — down from acuteLoad 806 on 2026-07-03 when readiness was scored 4 (POOR).

findings.claim: The one caveat on that recovery picture: total training volume over the last 17 days is 20.9 km, all of it in two sessions, and only one was a road run.
findings.value: 2026-08-22: 16.0 km road (last real session). Then nothing until 2026-09-02: 4.8 km (Soller, 25.5 min). 2026-09-05: 10.0 km treadmill + 6.09 km hiking. Between 08-23 and 09-01 inclusive: zero running, 10 consecutive days.
findings.derivation: summarizedActivities.json distinct activity days with distance/100000 and duration/60000. Corroborated in UDS by vigorousIntensityMinutes being 0 or 1 on every day from 08-23 through 09-01 except 09-01 itself at 12.

findings.claim: Hydration logging is worthless to rocket. It contains no hydration.
findings.value: 56 records, 100% hydrationSource = GARMIN_ACTIVITY, and valueInML is 0.0 on all 56 — the athlete has never logged a single drink. The only real number is estimatedSweatLossInML (76 to 3928 mL), which is a model output derived from an activity Garmin already gave rocket, not an observation.
findings.derivation: Both HydrationLogFiles; collections.Counter over hydrationSource, set() over valueInML, and every record carries an activityId. The same values re-appear inside UDS as the nested hydration object (53/161 records, valueInML always 0.0, goalInML constant 2839.056, adjustedGoalInML = goalInML + sweatLossInML). Skip both files.

findings.claim: Seven calendar days are not 24 hours long, which breaks any per-day rate calculation that divides by 86400.
findings.derivation: durationInMilliseconds / 3600000 across both UDSFiles. 2026-09-02 at 25 h coincides with averageMonitoringEnvironmentAltitude jumping to 312 m and a run named 'Soller Running' — a UTC+2 to UTC+1 return leg lengthening the local day. 2026-06-25 at 32 h has altitude 580 m, also travel. Always divide by durationInMilliseconds, never by a constant.

unitTraps: totalDistanceMeters / wellnessDistanceMeters are METRES, not centimetres. This is the opposite of summarizedActivities.json, where `distance` is centimetres. Verified two ways: implied stride (totalDistanceMeters/totalSteps) has median 0.846 m/step across 145 days, and on 2026-05-10 the UDS value 50597 sits just above the activity file's 42.70 km marathon-length run for the same day. A parser that reuses the activity-file centimetre assumption will under-report daily distance by 100x.
durationInMilliseconds is the length of the MEASUREMENT WINDOW, not a constant 86400000. Seven days are 11.0 h to 32.0 h. Never assume a 24 h day.

Timestamps in UDS are ISO STRINGS ('2026-03-28T00:00:00.0'), not epoch milliseconds — again the opposite of summarizedActivities.json. The single exception is restingHeartRateTimestamp, which IS epoch milliseconds (1774742400000 = 2026-03-29T00:00:00Z). Two timestamp conventions inside one record.

floorsAscendedInMeters / floorsDescendedInMeters are metres of vertical ascent, NOT floor counts. Only 31 of 144 non-zero values are exact multiples of 3.048 m (one Garmin floor), so the field is a genuine continuous metre measurement. Dividing by 3.048 to 'get floors' produces fractional garbage; multiplying by 3.048 to 'convert floors to metres' inflates by 3x.

highlyActiveSeconds and activeSeconds are SECONDS. moderateIntensityMinutes and vigorousIntensityMinutes are MINUTES. They are not convertible into each other: on 2026-03-28 highlyActiveSeconds/60 = 109 while vigorousIntensityMinutes = 83.

All allDayStress duration fields (stressDuration, activityDuration, uncategorizedDuration, totalDuration, lowDuration, mediumDuration, highDuration) are SECONDS. All allDayStress *Count fields are counts of 1-MINUTE samples — verified because totalDuration == totalStressCount * 60 on all 161 records. So stressOffWristCount 1436 means 1436 minutes = 23.9 h off wrist, not 1436 seconds.

averageStressLevel uses NEGATIVE SENTINELS: -1 means no data (13 days on the TOTAL aggregator), -2 means not measured (1 day on TOTAL, 159 days on the ASLEEP aggregator). Averaging these in drags the mean down by roughly 8 points. Null them before any aggregation.

restingHeartRate is a 7-DAY TRAILING MEAN, not a daily measurement. currentDayRestingHeartRate is the raw daily reading. Backfilling CTL/ATL-adjacent readiness from restingHeartRate silently applies a week of smoothing and will lag a taper by ~4 days.

bodyBattery.chargedValue and drainedValue do NOT reconcile with HIGHEST minus LOWEST — the overnight recharge straddles midnight and is credited across two calendar days. Use the HIGHEST/LOWEST stat entries, not the charge/drain arithmetic.
allDayStress.aggregatorList entries typed TOTAL and AWAKE are byte-identical on every record. Summing across the aggregator list double-counts everything.
dataQualityIssues: Both UDS filenames misstate their coverage. UDSFile_2026-02-20_2026-05-31.json contains nothing before 2026-03-28 (37 claimed days simply do not exist); UDSFile_2026-05-31_2026-09-08.json contains nothing on 2026-09-08. Trusting the filename dates would create 38 phantom empty days in a backfill.
3 dates have no record at all: 2026-08-29, 08-30, 08-31 — mid-holiday, watch presumably not worn or not synced.

15 further dates have a record but zero wellness data (totalSteps null, activeKilocalories 0, totalKilocalories pinned to the BMR floor of 2235): 2026-03-30, 04-01, 04-02, 04-06, 04-07, 04-08, 04-24, 05-03, 05-08, 05-15, 05-21, 05-25, 06-02, 06-17, 08-28. These must be treated as MISSING, not as zero-activity rest days — 2235 kcal with 0 steps is a modelled placeholder, not a measurement.

17 records omit the allDayStress duration keys entirely (stressDuration, lowDuration, mediumDuration, highDuration absent rather than null): the 15 watch-off dates above plus 2026-04-13, 07-03, 07-04. On 3 of those (04-13, 05-08, 05-15) averageStressLevel is nonetheless a plausible number (17, 16, 16) with no supporting duration — a value with no denominator. Do not trust those three.

7 days record a resting heart rate BELOW that day's own minimum heart rate, which is physically impossible: 2026-05-31, 06-07, 06-27, 07-05, 07-14, 07-26, 08-09. All are long-run days with anomalously high minHeartRate (63-76), meaning the watch was off overnight and the RHR was carried forward or modelled.
2026-05-21 records body battery HIGHEST = 98 and LOWEST = 98 with no steps and no heart-rate data — a single stale sample, not a real day. Same shape on 2026-06-02 (32/32) and 2026-08-28 (38/37).
2026-08-01 raw resting HR is 39 bpm against a smoothed 58 — a 19 bpm divergence, the largest in the export, on a 27270-step day. Almost certainly a single bad sample rather than a genuine reading.

restingHeartRate is present on only 143/161 days (88.8%), body battery stats on 151/161 (93.8%), respiration on 147/161 (91.3%), heart-rate extremes on 149/161 (92.5%). Steps and distance on 145/161 (90.1%). Calories and intensity minutes are the only metrics at 100%, and only because they fall back to a modelled BMR value.
42 of the 578 body-battery stat entries carry bodyBatteryStatus = MODELED rather than MEASURED — Garmin filled these in. Rocket should carry the status flag through rather than dropping it.
bodyBatteryFeedback (44% populated) contains only undecoded integer message IDs (feedbackLongType 300-588). There is no lookup table anywhere in the export. Unusable.

isVigorousDay is not derivable from vigorousIntensityMinutes and disagrees with it on at least 10 days (2026-04-20, 04-27, 04-28, 04-30, 05-06, 05-14, 05-17, 05-20, 05-23, 05-24). Its definition is opaque; do not ingest it.

Sleep stress is effectively absent: the ASLEEP aggregator reports the -2 no-data sentinel on 159 of 161 days. Any sleep-based readiness signal must come from the separate DI-Connect-Wellness sleepData files, not from UDS.
No SpO2 data anywhere: includesAllDayPulseOx and includesSleepPulseOx are false on all 161 records.
surprises: The brief's stated concern that the Garmin API only exposes ~42 days is understated for this domain, but in a different way than expected: the export gives 164 calendar days of daily wellness, NOT the full history. It begins 2026-03-28 — the day the watch was first worn — so there is no pre-March baseline at all. The March resting-HR figures (84-87 bpm) are a three-day untrained baseline, not a training-history datum.

The 86 bpm profile value is not merely stale — it is structurally frozen. heartRateZones.json carries restingHrAutoUpdateUsed = false, so Garmin has been computing HR zone floors (zone1 100, zone2 118, zone3 137, zone4 157, zone5 176) from RHR 86 while the athlete's actual resting HR has been 57-60 for four months. Every Karvonen-derived zone in the Garmin ecosystem is therefore wrong for this athlete, and any rocket logic that reads zone boundaries from Garmin inherits the error.

Body battery does NOT work as a next-day readiness signal, which is the opposite of how it is usually pitched. Correlation between a day's training load and the next morning's body battery peak is +0.091 — statistically nothing. After the three hardest sessions in the export (loads 462, 491, 340) the next-morning peaks were 88, 87 and 81, all within a point of the 80.1 all-time mean. The overnight recharge completely erases the session. Only the SAME-day trough carries signal (-0.415).
Pre-session stress carries no signal either (day-before mean 25.7 against an all-days mean near 26), so the whole 'check stress before a hard session' premise does not hold up in this athlete's data.

The single most informative readiness field turned out to be the one that looked like a duplicate: currentDayRestingHeartRate. It is the raw daily measurement and it is currently at 50 bpm (2026-09-07), while the field Garmin actually displays (restingHeartRate, a 7-day mean) still reads 57 and will not reflect the taper for another three or four days.

UDS coverage is anti-correlated with training, not correlated. The 23-day training blackout of May has almost complete wellness coverage; the three fully-absent days sit inside a holiday during which the athlete was still walking 12000+ steps a day. Coverage tracks whether the watch was worn, which tracks travel, not training.

2026-09-05 records 111 moderate intensity minutes — the highest single-day moderate figure in the entire export, on a day the athlete was supposedly barely training. It resolves to a 10 km treadmill run plus a 125-minute, 6.09 km hike. Rocket should not read the last fortnight as pure rest; there was a 2-hour aerobic block four days ago.

Hydration turned out to contain no hydration data whatsoever — valueInML is 0.0 on every one of the 56 records. The files are 100% auto-generated sweat-loss estimates keyed to activities rocket already has.
mined.rocketRelevance:
BACKFILL, but as a readiness sidecar — never as a load source. UDS contains no TSS, no training load, and no per-session data. CTL/ATL/TSB must come entirely from summarizedActivities.json; nothing in this domain feeds the 42-day and 7-day EWMAs, and nothing here feeds the Nielsen spike guardrail (which needs per-session distance, not daily totals). Do not let daily totalDistanceMeters leak into the spike calculation: on 2026-05-10 it reads 50597 m against a 42.70 km run, and a guardrail fed the daily figure would compute a 110% ceiling that is 18% too generous.

WHAT TO BACKFILL (161 rows, 2026-03-28 to 2026-09-07, keyed on calendarDate):
1. currentDayRestingHeartRate as the daily resting-HR series — the raw measurement, 143 rows. Store restingHeartRate separately and LABEL it as Garmin's 7-day mean; do not let the two collapse into one column. Null the raw value on the 7 dates where it falls below minHeartRate.
2. bodyBattery LOWEST + HIGHEST + the MEASURED/RESET/MODELED status, 151 rows. Use LOWEST as a session-cost marker (correlation -0.415 with same-day load, median 22 on hard days versus 42 overall). Do NOT build a next-day readiness feature on HIGHEST — it has no predictive power here (+0.091).
3. allDayStress TOTAL averageStressLevel with the -1/-2 sentinels nulled, plus stressOffWristCount as the wear-time/data-quality flag. The off-wrist count is the cheapest way to distinguish a genuine rest day from a not-worn day.
4. totalSteps and totalDistanceMeters as non-run load context — useful for spotting the 12000-step "rest" days that are not actually rest.
5. moderateIntensityMinutes / vigorousIntensityMinutes as an independent completeness oracle on the activity backfill. Verified: zero UDS days with vigorousIntensityMinutes >= 25 lack an activity record, and zero activity days lack a UDS record. If that invariant breaks after ingest, the activity backfill dropped a session.

CROSS-CHECK, DO NOT INGEST: the 86 bpm resting HR in heartRateZones.json. It is frozen (restingHrAutoUpdateUsed = false) and 28 bpm above the current measured value, so every Garmin-derived HR zone for this athlete is wrong. If rocket's race-day rule "take it to 4:35/km if heart rate is under 170 at 10 km" was set against Garmin zones, that 170 threshold deserves re-derivation from the athlete's own lactateThresholdHeartRate of 177 (userBioMetricProfileData.json) and measured RHR of ~58, not from the 86-based zone table.

IGNORE ENTIRELY: both HydrationLogFiles and the nested hydration object (valueInML is 0.0 on all 56 records — there is no logged intake, only model output derived from activities rocket already has); bodyBatteryFeedback (undecoded integer message IDs, no lookup table in the export); isVigorousDay (opaque, disagrees with vigorousIntensityMinutes on 10+ days); the wellness* duplicate fields (wellnessKilocalories, wellnessTotalKilocalories, wellnessActiveKilocalories, wellnessDistanceMeters — all byte-identical to their non-prefixed twins); the AWAKE stress aggregator (identical to TOTAL); the ASLEEP aggregator (-2 sentinel on 159/161 days).

IMMEDIATE OPERATIONAL READ, 4 days from Battersea Half: raw resting HR 50 bpm on 2026-09-07 is the lowest since 2026-08-01 and 7-9 bpm under the summer baseline; body battery never fell below 72 all day (joint 4th-highest trough of 151 measured days, median 42); average stress 14 against a mean near 26. mined.schemaNotes:
NAMING: `luisdeburnaybastos@gmail.com_<uploadId>.fit`. The numeric part is a Garmin UPLOAD id (12 digits, e.g. 436653166210), NOT the activityId in summarizedActivities.json (11 digits, e.g. 22832542087). Zero overlap between the two id sets — do not join on filename. Join on time: file_id.time_created (UTC datetime) == summarizedActivities startTimeGmt/1000 (epoch seconds UTC). Max observed offset over 56 pairs = 1.0 s.

FORMAT: genuine FIT binary. Header 14 B (0x0E), ".FIT" ASCII at offset 8, header CRC at 12-13, file CRC in last 2 B. All 1803 parse with fitparse 1.2 with zero errors. Every file: manufacturer=garmin, garmin_product=4536, serial_number=3613943939 (one device, whole corpus). The `.bak` in device-backups is NOT a FIT — magic is `PK\x03\x04`, it is a ZIP containing `2/Settings.fit`, `15/0.bin` and ~40 `5/<SportProfile>.fit` sport-profile files.

ACTIVITY FILE MESSAGE SHAPE (per file): file_id, file_creator, device_info (x12), device_settings, user_profile, sport, zones_target, timestamp_correlation, session (x1), lap (xN), event (xN), record (xN), gps_metadata (~= record count, GPS activities only), plus Garmin-private globals unknown_233 (~record count), unknown_534 (== record count), unknown_325/326/327, unknown_216, unknown_104 (== lap count).

RECORD FIELDS (named, all 100% covered on GPS runs unless noted): timestamp (datetime), position_lat/position_long (semicircles, fitparse yields raw int), distance (METRES, cumulative float), enhanced_speed (M/S — verified below), enhanced_altitude (m), heart_rate (bpm), cadence (rpm, one-leg) + fractional_cadence, power (W, Garmin running power), accumulated_power (J), activity_type. Running dynamics at 93-98%: vertical_oscillation, vertical_ratio, step_length, stance_time. Unnamed-but-present: unknown_87/90/107/135/136/137/138/140/143/145.

SESSION FIELDS: start_time (datetime), total_distance (METRES float), total_elapsed_time (SECONDS float), total_timer_time (SECONDS float), total_calories, total_ascent (m), avg_heart_rate, max_heart_rate, num_laps, sport, sub_sport. NOTE avg_speed / max_speed / enhanced_avg_speed are None in this corpus — derive speed yourself from total_distance/total_timer_time.

EVENT MESSAGES: `event='timer'` with `event_type` in {start, stop_all} ONLY (no 'stop', no 'pause' variants) — 57 start + 57 stop_all as the outer bracket, plus paired start/stop_all for each pause. Other event subtypes seen: speed_low_alert (start/stop), and one `event=39, event_type=marker, data=98`.

UNIT MAP, FIT vs summarizedActivities.json (factor to multiply FIT by to get JSON):
  session.total_distance (m)      -> distance (cm)             x100
  session.total_elapsed_time (s)  -> elapsedDuration (ms)      x1000
  session.total_timer_time (s)    -> duration (ms)             x1000
  record.enhanced_speed (m/s)     -> avgSpeed (cm/ms)          /10
  session.avg_heart_rate          -> avgHr                     x1 (exact match, 56/56)

unitTraps: FIT session.total_distance is METRES (10000.0 = 10.00 km). summarizedActivities.json distance is CENTIMETRES (1000000.0 = 10.00 km). Factor 100 between the two — do not reuse the JSON's cm assumption when reading FIT.
FIT total_elapsed_time / total_timer_time are SECONDS as floats. The JSON's elapsedDuration / duration are MILLISECONDS. Factor 1000.
JSON `duration` is timer (moving) time, NOT elapsed. Treating it as elapsed silently removes every pause from the timeline. `elapsedDuration` is the elapsed one. Verified to 0.4 ms on all 56 pairs.

JSON `movingDuration` is a THIRD value, always <= timer time (mean 255 s less, max 7214 s less on the LA hike). It is Garmin's own low-speed-excluding computation and matches nothing in the FIT. Do not use it as either elapsed or moving time for load — it has no FIT counterpart to validate against.

record.enhanced_speed is m/s. Verified by integrating speed*dt over 2954 1-Hz records of the 2026-09-05 treadmill = 7488.7 m against final cumulative record.distance = 7488.68 m. The JSON's avgSpeed is that value divided by 10 (cm/ms): treadmill JSON avgSpeed=0.3386 vs FIT-derived 10000.0 m / 2953.512 s = 3.3858 m/s; Leeds JSON avgSpeed=0.3014 vs 42666.89/14154.025 = 3.0145 m/s. Confirmed on two files.
session.avg_speed, max_speed and enhanced_avg_speed are None throughout this corpus. Compute speed from total_distance/total_timer_time; do not read the session speed fields.
record dt is 1 s for runs but ~3 s for hikes (smart recording). Any per-second integration must weight by actual timestamp delta.
record.distance is cumulative, not per-sample. record.accumulated_power is cumulative joules, not watts.
position_lat/position_long are FIT semicircles; multiply by 180/2^31 for degrees. fitparse returns the raw integer here, not degrees.
dataQualityIssues: 2026-09-05 treadmill (activityId 24251846565): session and summarized distance say 10000.00 m; the record stream and its own speed integral both say 7488.68 m. A 33.5% inflation carried into summarizedActivities.json. Almost certainly a post-hoc treadmill calibration.

summarizedActivities.json is stale by one activity: a 7.65 km run on 2026-09-07 19:09 UTC exists as a raw FIT (479581793159) but has no summarized entry. An ingest keyed off the export JSON will silently drop it.
40 type-41 FIT files have file_id.time_created == None, so they cannot be placed on a timeline. Not activity data, but noted.
Hiking files use smart recording (median 3 s sampling), so their record streams are not comparable to running files without dt weighting.

The 2026-07-03 LA hike (456201578440) records timer 10014 s over a 3.75 km hike, of which Garmin's movingDuration claims only 2800 s. avg HR 92. It is a walk, not training load, and will distort ATL if ingested at face value alongside runs.
device-backups .bak has a .bak extension but ZIP magic bytes — anything that dispatches on extension will hand it to a FIT parser and get 'Invalid .FIT File Header'.
surprises: The brief describes the export's units as centimetres/milliseconds throughout. Inside the FIT files they are metres and seconds. The cm/ms convention is specific to summarizedActivities.json, not to the export.

The brief implies the cropper is the reason to want raw files. It is not: pause time is already exactly derivable from the summarized JSON as elapsedDuration - duration (verified to 0.4 ms on all 56). The raw files' real added value is per-second HR/power/dynamics and the ability to catch summary corruption.

1803 FIT files, but only 57 are activities. 987 are daily monitoring and 701 are an undocumented type-44. The 13.5 MB 'largest payload' is 69% activity data by uncompressed bytes but only 3% by file count.
There are 57 activity FITs, not 56 — one run (2026-09-07) postdates the summarized snapshot.
The named target file for the treadmill run does not actually record 10.00 km. The headline figure in the brief is the corrected value, not the measured one.
Both named target files have zero pauses, so they are the two worst possible choices for demonstrating the cropper.

mined.rocketRelevance:
BACKFILL THEM — but not for the reason the brief assumes, and the summarized JSON stays the primary source for CTL/ATL/TSB.

What the summarized JSON already covers, exactly: distance, elapsed time, timer time, avg/max HR all reconcile against the FIT sessions to 0.01 m and 0.4 ms across all 56 activities. Pause time is elapsedDuration - duration, no FIT needed. So the load engine's core inputs need no raw-file backfill, and the pause-cropper adds nothing to CTL/ATL — it is a Strava-shipping tool, not a load-engine input.

What only the raw files give you, and why it is worth 21.2 MB and 200,098 records:

1. Defensible session TSS. The summary gives one avgHr per activity. The FITs give 200,098 per-second HR samples plus Garmin running power at 100% coverage. That is the difference between a duration x avg-intensity approximation and a real TRIMP or normalized-power-based TSS. With a 5-week 60/80/100/80/60 km build starting in six days, the difference between those two shows up as a systematically wrong ATL on the 100 km week.

2. Interval structure. The summary has no lap data. Leeds has 43 laps, the treadmill has 8. Without laps, a 21 km steady run and a 21 km session with 10x1 km reps produce identical load. They should not.

3. A cross-check that catches summary corruption. This is the concrete, immediate one. The 2026-09-05 treadmill run — the most recent hard session, four days before Battersea Half — is recorded in summarizedActivities.json as 10.00 km when the sensor stream says 7.49 km. Ingesting the summary alone puts a phantom 2.5 km into the trailing-30-day window and a phantom 4:55/km into the pace history. The single-session spike guardrail (110% of the longest run in the trailing 30 days) is computed off exactly this number. The raw file is the only thing in the export that detects it, and routr's inspect_fit.py detects it automatically via summary reconciliation.

Concrete ingest recipe:
- Join FIT to activity on file_id.time_created (UTC) vs startTimeGmt/1000, tolerance 2 s. Never on filename — those are upload ids and match nothing.
- On ingest, run the summary-reconciliation check (session.total_distance vs final record.distance). Flag anything with ratio outside 1.00 +/- 0.01. Exactly one activity fails today; quarantine 24251846565's distance rather than trusting it.
- Ingest the 2026-09-07 run (479581793159) separately — it is real training load that the summarized JSON does not contain.
- Weight per-second integrations by actual timestamp delta; hikes sample at 3 s.
- Consider excluding sport=hiking from ATL entirely, or down-weighting it: the two hikes contribute 4.8 h of timer time at avg HR 92 and 106.

Do NOT bother with: the device-backups, PrimaryTrainingBackup, LhaBackup or ECG zips (no session/lap/record messages anywhere in them), or the 1746 non-activity FITs unless rocket later wants resting HR / sleep / HRV, which live in the 987 monitoring_b files and are a separate domain.

Toolchain: routr's inspect_fit.py and crop_fit_pauses.py both run against these files unmodified — inspector clean on the two GPS files tested, cropper's dry-run found 72 pauses totalling 2292 s against a session-derived 2296.5 s. fitparse >= 1.2 is the only dependency. mined.schemaNotes:
personalRecord.json — top level is a LIST of one object with key `personalRecords`; the array is at d[0]["personalRecords"]. Row fields: personalRecordId (int), activityId (int, 0 for non-activity PRs), value (float, POLYMORPHIC — see unitTraps), prStartTimeGMT (string, Java Date.toString format "Sat May 09 23:00:00 GMT 2026" — parse with "%a %b %d %H:%M:%S GMT %Y", NOT epoch ms like summarizedActivities), personalRecordType (string, free text label), createdDate (string "YYYY-MM-DD", the day Garmin wrote the row, not the day of the effort), current (bool — the live PR for that type), confirmed (bool, all true). personalRecordType values seen: "Best 1km Run", "Best 1mile Run", "Best 5km Run", "Best 10km Run", "Best Half Marathon", "Best Full Marathon", "Farthest Run", "Most Steps in a Day", "Most Steps in a Week", "Most Steps in a Month", "Current Goal Streak", "Longest Goal Streak". No sport field beyond the label; no pace, no HR, no elevation. History is append-only: superseded PRs stay with current:false, so the file doubles as a progression timeline.

weekly_training_report.json — d[0]["weeklyTrainingReportExport"] is a list of 4 objects keyed by primaryActivityType. Each has weeklyTrainingReportSections[] {weeklyTrainingReportSectionType, sectionEnabled, isEditable, webSort, mobileSort, weeklyTrainingReportSectionItems[]{weeklyTrainingReportSectionItemType, enabled, sortOrder}} plus crossTrainingEnabled. Every leaf is a string, a bool, or a small int sort index (only integers present anywhere in the file are 0-6). It is a UI layout preference blob, not a report.

UserGoal_2025-12-19_2026-03-29.json — list of {userProfilePk, userGoalCategory, userGoalType, startDate{date}, goalValue (STRING, "11130.0"), updateDate{date}, createDate{date}}. Dates are human strings ("Mar 28, 2026", "Sep 7, 2026 12:00:00 AM"), not ISO, not epoch. Filename date range 2025-12-19_2026-03-29 does not match the content window — do not parse the filename as a data span.

customer.json — flat object. Useful fields: dateOfBirth "1998-11-13" (ISO), locale "en_GB", customerLocation.countryCode "GB", createdDate "2026-03-28T18:46:24Z", accountVerified true. ISO-8601 Z timestamps here, unlike everything in DI-Connect.

devicesandcontent.json — {"deviceAndContentInfo":[{"Devices":[{unitId, serialNumber, partNumber, registrationDate}]}]}. Note the capitalised "Devices" key. registrationDate is a human string "March 28, 2026".

unitTraps: personalRecord.json `value` is POLYMORPHIC and the file gives no unit field — you must branch on personalRecordType. Seconds (float) for Best 1km/1mile/5km/10km/Half Marathon/Full Marathon. METRES (float) for Farthest Run. Raw count for Most Steps in a Day/Week/Month. Days (float) for Current/Longest Goal Streak. A parser that applies one unit across the file will produce a 42,666-second 'marathon' or an 11.9-metre 'farthest run'.

DISTANCE UNIT FLIPS BETWEEN FILES. personalRecord.json Farthest Run = 42666.890625 METRES. summarizedActivities.json distance for the same activity = 4266689.0625 CENTIMETRES. Same physical run, factor of 100 apart. Do not reuse a summarizedActivities distance parser here.

TIME UNIT ALSO FLIPS. personalRecord.json values are SECONDS (6284.099). summarizedActivities.json duration is MILLISECONDS (6284099.121). Factor of 1000. The two match exactly for activity 23744064058, which is how I confirmed both.

prStartTimeGMT is NOT epoch milliseconds, unlike beginTimestamp/startTimeGmt/startTimeLocal in summarizedActivities. It is a Java Date.toString() string: "Sat May 09 23:00:00 GMT 2026". Format string "%a %b %d %H:%M:%S GMT %Y". Feeding it to a ms-epoch parser fails; feeding it to a naive ISO parser also fails.

Aggregate PR dates are LOCAL MIDNIGHT EXPRESSED AS GMT, so they read one day early under British Summer Time. "Most Steps in a Day" prStartTimeGMT = Sat May 09 23:00:00 GMT 2026 means the local day 2026-05-10. Bucketing these by GMT calendar date puts every step PR in the wrong day.

createdDate on a PR row is the day Garmin WROTE the record, not the day of the effort. Row 2884514863 has createdDate 2026-03-28 and prStartTimeGMT 2026-03-28 (same), but row 2887023027 has createdDate 2026-03-31 for an effort on 2026-03-29. Always use prStartTimeGMT for the effort date.
UserGoal goalValue is a STRING containing a float: "11130.0", not 11130. Numeric comparison without a cast silently fails.

RunRacePredictions raceTime* fields are INTEGER SECONDS with no unit suffix — 5905 is 1:38:25, not 5905 ms and not 59.05 anything. Verified two ways: 5905 s / 21.0975 km = 4:39.7/km, a plausible half pace, and the same file's raceTime5K 1213 s = 20:13, consistent with the 5 km PR of 19:40.

Some PR values are the whole parent activity's duration and some are a rolling window inside it. Half PR 6284.099 s == activity 23744064058's full duration; marathon PR 13984.818 s is 169.2 s SHORTER than activity 22832542087's full duration. Do not assume PR == activity time, and do not assume PR < activity time either.
dataQualityIssues: DUPLICATE PR ROWS FOR ONE ACTIVITY. personalRecordIds 2909775686 (value 6908.320 s) and 2909775687 (value 6686.411 s) are both personalRecordType "Best Half Marathon", both activityId 22667722940, both prStartTimeGMT 2026-04-26 13:10 (36 seconds apart). 6686.411 s exactly equals that activity's duration (6686411.13 ms in summarizedActivities.json) while 6908.320 s does not correspond to anything — Garmin appears to have written both a window figure and an activity figure. Any 'count of PRs' or 'best per activity' aggregation must dedupe on (personalRecordType, activityId).

Garmin awarded a Half Marathon PR on a run measured at 21,096.49 m — 1.01 m SHORT of the 21,097.5 m half-marathon distance (activity 23744064058). Either Garmin uses a tolerance or a different internal distance stream than the exported `distance` field. Immaterial for pace but it means the PR is not provably over the full distance.

"Most Steps in a Month" has prStartTimeGMT of Wed Aug 26 23:00 GMT (local 2026-08-27), which is not the start of any calendar month. Either it is a rolling 30-day window or the timestamp means something other than period-start. Do not interpret the monthly step PR as a calendar-month figure without resolving this.

UserGoal filename is UserGoal_2025-12-19_2026-03-29.json but the single row inside has startDate Mar 28 2026 and updateDate Sep 7 2026 — the content extends five months past the filename's end date. Filename date ranges in DI-Connect-User are unreliable as data spans.

customer.json has gender: null and displayName: null. dateOfBirth 1998-11-13 is present (athlete is 27), but if rocket's load model ever wants a sex-specific or HRmax-by-age term, sex is not in this export.

The two 2026-09-07 consent grants are identified only by opaque UUIDs. This export contains no consent-type dictionary, so what was actually consented to cannot be established from the data — only from Garmin's developer portal.

personalRecord.json holds no PR for any distance between 10 km and 21.1 km, and none above the marathon. There is also no 3 km, no 2 mile, and no 'Best Effort' pace/power series. It is a sparse set of six run distances only.
surprises: The brief frames this export as 'the full history' versus the ~42-day Garmin API window. It is full, but full is short: the account was created 2026-03-28T18:46:24Z and the first activity is 2026-03-28T20:25:27Z, so there are only 163 days and 56 activities in total. The backfill extends rocket's window from ~42 days to ~163 days, not to years. A 42-day CTL EWMA needs roughly 3-4 time constants (~126-170 days) to settle, so this history is only just long enough to produce a trustworthy CTL — and only from about 2026-08 onward.

The weekly training report is not a report. The brief asks whether it holds a load figure rocket could reuse; it holds no numbers at all beyond UI sort indices. It is a display-preferences blob. The OVERALL_TRAINING_LOAD item it lists is a section the athlete has switched on, not a value.

gear.json is not empty in the `[]` sense — it is `[{}]`, a list containing one empty object. So are trainingPlan.json and workout.json. A parser that checks `if data:` will treat all three as non-empty and then fail on missing keys. user_reminders.json is the genuinely-empty one at `[]` (2 bytes, not 4).

The half-marathon PR is a paused training run, not a race. 16m 02s of stopped time (elapsed 7245.7 s vs moving 6284.1 s). rocket should not treat 1:44:44 as a race-day benchmark — it is a moving-time figure from a stop-start run, and the real race capability is better represented by Garmin's 1:38:25 prediction.

The 10 km PR (4:37.9/km) is SLOWER per kilometre than a Riegel extrapolation from the 5 km PR (~4:06/km) predicts, by 12.9%. The athlete has a genuine 5 km time trial and a genuine marathon, but has apparently never raced a 10 km. Any model that fits a critical-speed or Riegel curve across all PRs will be dragged slow by this one point.

There is no Garmin-side training plan at all (trainingPlan.json empty, no race goal in UserGoal). rocket is not overriding or conflicting with anything the watch is prescribing — but it also means the watch's daily suggested workouts, if used, are unrecorded here.

Consent to share with Strava has been live since 2026-03-28, i.e. before rocket existed. rocket's ship-to-Strava step is not creating a new data-sharing relationship, it is using one the athlete established on day one.

Every prediction row and every activity comes from one device (deviceId 3613943939, a fenix 8) registered on the account's creation day. There is no device swap, so no calibration discontinuity to model in the backfill — unusual and convenient.
mined.rocketRelevance:
"Backfill from this domain: only personalRecord.json. Load the 36 activity-linked run PRs (activityId != 0) as a benchmark table keyed on (personalRecordType, activityId) with dedupe, storing the six current:true run PRs as the athlete's live bests and the current:false rows as a progression series. Value parsing must branch on personalRecordType per the unit traps. Every PR row carries an activityId that joins to summarizedActivities.json, so the PR table can be reconstructed from activities if it is ever suspect — treat personalRecord.json as a convenience index, not a primary source.

IGNORE for backfill: weekly_training_report.json (UI preferences, zero measurements — nothing for CTL/ATL/TSB), gear.json, trainingPlan.json, workout.json, user_reminders.json (all empty), devicesandcontent.json and customer.json (identity only; dateOfBirth 1998-11-13 is the one field with modelling use, if an age-based HRmax is ever wanted).

CROSS-CHECK against: (1) The spike guardrail — the longest run in the trailing 30 days should be validated against Farthest Run PRs; the 42.667 km on 2026-05-10 is the all-time max, and 110% of it (46.93 km) is a ceiling no session in the 5-week build should approach. Note that this PR is 121 days stale, so the 30-day trailing max on race week will be far lower and the guardrail correspondingly tighter. (2) Race-day pacing for 2026-09-12 — the three numbers rocket should surface are PR 1:44:44 (4:57.9/km, but from a paused training run), Garmin prediction 1:38:25 (4:39.7/km, from RunRacePredictions dated 2026-09-07), and the plan of 4:45/km opening = 1:40:13, taking it to 4:35/km = 1:36:42 if HR is under 170 at 10 km. The plan is faster than the PR and straddles the prediction, so it is aggressive-but-defensible rather than reckless — worth saying explicitly, because 'PR is 1:44 and you plan to run 1:40' looks alarming until you see the prediction. The HR-170 trigger is well-chosen: the 2026-07-26 half ran at avgHr 165 / maxHr 190, so 170 at 10 km is a genuine discriminator, not a formality. (3) The 42-day API window rocket already has covers 2026-07-28 onward; the PRs set on 2026-07-02, 2026-07-12 and 2026-07-26 all fall OUTSIDE it, so the current 1 km, 1 mile, 10 km and half PRs were invisible to rocket before this export.

Operational note: gear tracking is confirmed unused on Garmin, so rocket cannot source shoe mileage from any Garmin sync — the athlete's manual daily-trainer / carbon-race-shoe split has no upstream to reconcile against, and if rocket wants shoe mileage it must own that store entirely.

Data-handling constraint: nothing in consentHistory.json restricts rocket. All four consents are self-granted, GRANTED, and non-expiring; there is no revocation and no processing limitation expressed. The Strava consent that rocket's ship-to-Strava flow relies on has been live since 2026-03-28. The caveat is that the two 2026-09-07 partner consents are opaque UUIDs with no type dictionary in the export, so what they authorise cannot be read from this data — if rocket's ingest poller depends on a specific Garmin developer-API scope, confirm it in the Garmin developer portal rather than inferring it from these rows."

mined.domain: Saved courses and routes (Garmin Connect route planner) — DI-Connect-Routing
mined.recordCounts: 40 course objects, 40,421 geoPoints total, 506.58 km of drawn geometry. createDate span 2026-03-31T19:37:03 to 2026-09-02T03:49:21 (155 days). Point counts per course range 255 ("529", 5.24 km) to 2564 ("30 bags", 30.50 km). 35 courseType="running", 5 "hiking". All 40 accessControl="private", all hasTurnDetectionDisabled=false. createDate==updateDate for 36 of 40; 4 were later edited.
mined.schemaNotes:
Top level is a JSON ARRAY of 40 course objects (not an envelope). Exactly 10 keys, present on all 40 — no optional fields, no nesting beyond geoPoints:

- courseName: string, free text. Two shapes: athlete-typed ("12km", "30 bags", "SUNDAYBABY", "I'm feeling 22") and Garmin-autogenerated street concatenations ("The Hyde-High Street-Edgwarebury Lane").
- courseType: string enum, only two values observed: "running" (35), "hiking" (5). This is the athlete's chosen activity type, NOT a surface classification.
- accessControl: string, "private" for all 40.
- hasTurnDetectionDisabled: boolean, false for all 40.
- createDate / updateDate: ISO-8601 LOCAL-TIME STRINGS, not epoch ms — "2026-03-31T19:37:03.0". No timezone suffix, no offset. Fractional-second field is always ".0". This is the one place the export departs from the epoch-milliseconds convention seen in summarizedActivities.json; do not apply the ms-epoch parser here.
- elevationGainMeter / elevationLossMeter: float, METRES (verified, see findings). Gain and loss are NOT equal on all courses (they are equal on 2 of 40 exactly), so these are genuinely computed, not mirrored.
- startPoint: object {latitude, longitude, elevation} — a duplicate of geoPoints[0] in every course checked. Redundant.
- geoPoints: array of {latitude: float, longitude: float, elevation: float}. All three keys present on all 40,421 points; zero nulls, zero missing.

GEOMETRY ENCODING: raw decimal-degree coordinate arrays. NOT an encoded polyline, NOT base64, NOT delta-compressed. lat/lon carry 14-15 decimal places (float64 noise from Garmin's internal fixed-point representation — real precision is ~7 dp). elevation is metres to 2 dp.

NOT PRESENT — the significant absences:
- No distance field at any level. Course length must be derived from geoPoints.
- No surface / terrain / road-type field anywhere.
- No per-point timestamp, no cumulative-distance, no grade — geoPoints are pure geometry.
- No course ID, UUID, or Garmin courseId. courseName is the only identifier, and it is not unique (4 duplicate-name/duplicate-geometry pairs).
- No link to any activity: nothing says whether a course was ever actually run.
- No estimated duration, no target pace, no workout steps.

findings.claim: Total drawn distance across all 40 courses
findings.derivation: No distance field exists in the file. Summed haversine (R=6371008.8 m, WGS84 mean radius) over consecutive geoPoints for each course, then summed the 40 course totals. Independent cross-check: the athlete self-labels many courses with their intended distance, and derived values track those labels — "12km"->11.92, "21km"->21.08, "15km"->14.72, "8.5km"->8.48, "13"->13.06, "11.75"->11.73, "5k"->5.41, "30 bags"->30.50. Agreement within a few percent across 15+ independently-named courses confirms the haversine sum is in metres and the coordinates are plain decimal degrees.

findings.claim: elevationGainMeter is metres of threshold-filtered ascent, not raw point-to-point ascent
findings.value: 1.0 m hysteresis threshold reconciles it; mean absolute error 3.41 m across 40 courses
findings.derivation: Summed raw positive elevation deltas over geoPoints and compared to the stated elevationGainMeter. Raw sum overshoots on every course (mean abs error 11.03 m; e.g. "30 bags" stated 371.6 vs raw 395.7). Re-ran with a hysteresis filter at thresholds 0.0/0.5/1.0/2.0/3.0 m: mean abs error was 11.03 / 6.49 / 3.41 / 6.79 / 11.35. The 1.0 m minimum converges, confirming both the unit (metres) and Garmin's filtering convention. Recompute rather than trusting the field if you need consistency with your own elevation maths.

findings.claim: Per-point elevation is present on every point and is DEM-derived, not barometric
findings.value: 40,421 of 40,421 points carry elevation; range 2.87 m to 368.27 m; zero nulls, zero zeros
findings.derivation: Counted elevation keys across all geoPoints (union count == total point count). min/max over the flattened list. These are planned routes with no recorded pressure data, so elevation can only come from Garmin's terrain model sampled along the drawn line — which also explains why it is smooth enough that a 1 m threshold is needed to match the stated gain.

findings.claim: Point density is dense and near-uniform — well inside what GraphHopper map-matching needs
findings.value: Median inter-point gap 9.8 m corpus-wide; p90 ~25 m; per-course medians 6.9-14.9 m (one outlier at 21.0 m)
findings.derivation: Per-course haversine step lengths, zero-length steps excluded, median and 90th-percentile taken. 38 of 40 courses have a median gap between 6.9 and 14.9 m. Only "Running 21 Aug" differs (uniform 21.0 m median, min 0.61 m, max 34.96 m). Max single gaps reach 225-393 m on five courses, which are straight-line segments the planner drew without intermediate vertices, not data loss.

unitTraps: createDate / updateDate are ISO-8601 LOCAL-TIME STRINGS ("2026-03-31T19:37:03.0"), NOT epoch milliseconds. This directly contradicts the convention in summarizedActivities.json. A parser that assumes ms-epoch across the export will throw or produce garbage here. There is no timezone offset — the values are naive local time and cannot be converted to UTC from this file alone.

elevationGainMeter / elevationLossMeter are METRES (not centimetres, unlike `distance` in summarizedActivities.json). Verified independently by summing per-point elevation deltas, which are also plain metres. Do NOT apply the centimetre divisor here.

elevationGainMeter is threshold-FILTERED ascent (1 m hysteresis), not the raw sum of positive deltas. Raw summation overshoots Garmin's figure by 5-10% on every course. If rocket computes elevation load itself, it will systematically disagree with the Garmin figure unless the same threshold is applied.

There is NO distance field. Any pipeline expecting one will silently read null. Distance must be derived by haversine over geoPoints — and derived distance is the length of the DRAWN LINE, which is not the same thing as a distance actually run.

lat/lon carry 14-15 decimal places. That is float64 representation noise, not precision — real fidelity is ~7 dp (~1 cm). Do not treat the trailing digits as meaningful, and do not use exact float equality for deduplication except where checking for Garmin's own repeated join vertices (which ARE bit-identical).
startPoint duplicates geoPoints[0] but its elevation is rounded to the same 2 dp — it is redundant, not an independent reading. Do not treat it as a separate data point.

courseType ("running" / "hiking") is the athlete's activity-type selection, NOT a surface or terrain classification. The 5 "hiking" courses include "The Hyde-High Street-Edgwarebury Lane", a 15.7 km suburban street route. Reading courseType as a trail/road proxy would be wrong.
dataQualityIssues: Four duplicate/near-duplicate course pairs (detailed in findings). Two are byte-identical geometry saved twice. Deduplication must be on geometry hash — courseName is neither unique nor stable (one pair has different names for identical geometry).
No stable identifier. courseName is the only handle and it collides. Any ingest needs a synthetic key (e.g. hash of rounded geoPoints) and must be idempotent across re-exports.

No link between a course and any activity. The file cannot tell you whether a route was run once, fifty times, or never. Correlating a course to actual sessions requires spatial matching against activity tracks in DI-Connect-Fitness — that work does not exist yet.

Five courses contain single inter-point gaps of 180-393 m ("12km" 343.7 m, "longRun 2" 392.6 m, "I'm feeling 22" 387.2 m, "A19km" 386.9 m, "test route" 213.2 m, "Maplebeck Road..." 225.0 m). These are straight-line planner segments drawn without intermediate vertices — the drawn line may cut across terrain rather than follow a way. Map-matching will either bridge them via the road graph (inflating distance vs the drawn line) or fail. These six courses are the ones most likely to trip routr's inflation guard.
1,082 zero-length steps (duplicate consecutive vertices) across the corpus. Contribute nothing to distance but should be stripped before map-matching.

createDate has no timezone. The Mallorca and Los Angeles courses were created while the athlete was abroad, so their local timestamps are on a different offset from the London ones with no way to tell from this file. Sequencing courses across the travel blocks by raw string sort introduces up to 8 hours of error.
surprises: The brief warned that the export is uniformly treacherous on units — centimetres, milliseconds, epoch-ms timestamps. This file is the exception: it is entirely in SI base units (metres, decimal degrees) and its timestamps are ISO-8601 local-time strings. The trap here is the opposite of the one expected: applying the summarizedActivities.json conventions to this file is what breaks it.

There is no distance field at all. Given that every course is named after its distance by the athlete ("12km", "21km", "30 bags"), the absence of the one number the athlete cares about is striking. Garmin computes it client-side.

Nothing in the corpus goes anywhere near Battersea Park — nearest approach 5.59 km, and no GB course reaches south of 51.5291 N. With the half marathon 4 days out and the marathon at the same venue, the athlete has never drawn or previewed the race route. That is a genuine gap, not a data artefact.

The geometry is already road-snapped by Garmin's own planner (median 9.8 m spacing, vertices doubled at way junctions, elevation sampled from a DEM). These are not GPS traces. routr's gpx_match.py docstring says its one fixture that matched exactly on the first attempt was the one whose points were already on the graph — these courses are that shape, which is a better outcome than the brief's framing of "could be fed through routr" implies.

A 32.55 km course in Nottinghamshire ("Maplebeck Road-Ossington Road-Caunton Road", 2026-04-05) and a 31.11 km "longRun 2" (2026-04-12) exist from April — marathon-distance-adjacent route planning was happening five months before the goal race, at a point the 5-week build had not started.
mined.rocketRelevance:
IGNORE for the current phase. Do not backfill this domain now.

Straight answer: these are PLANNED routes, not executed sessions. The load engine needs completed work — duration, distance actually covered, and an intensity proxy — to feed CTL (42-day EWMA), ATL (7-day EWMA) and TSB. This file has no date-run, no duration, no heart rate, no pace, and no link to any activity. It cannot contribute a single training-load data point. Feeding drawn-course distances into the load engine would be actively harmful: it would credit the athlete with 506.58 km of work that may never have happened, corrupting CTL and inflating the 30-day longest-run baseline that the Nielsen spike guardrail (110% of trailing-30-day longest run) is computed from. Note specifically that \"30 bags\" (30.50 km) and \"Maplebeck Road...\" (32.55 km) would each raise that ceiling by ~10 km if mistaken for completed runs. The guardrail must draw its longest-run figure from activities only.

What it IS good for, later:
1. Surface profiling via routr (phase 2). Run the 36 distinct courses through routr's /api/classify to learn the athlete's actual road/gravel/trail/path mix. That informs shoe choice and the injury-risk model. It is real value and the conversion cost is near zero — but it is a nicety, and the half marathon is 4 days away.
2. Route suggestion (phase 2+). Once rocket prescribes \"80 km week, 22 km long run\", a library of the athlete's own known-good routes indexed by derived distance is directly useful — there are courses at 2.96, 5.2-6.3 (x9), 8.5, 9.5-10.6 (x5), 11.4-12.1 (x4), 13.1, 14.7, 15.7, 17.5, 19.7, 21.1-22.6 (x4), 30.5 and 32.6 km. That covers the prescribed distances well.
3. One immediate, non-ingest action worth taking now: the athlete has no Battersea Park course. With two races there in the next 7 weeks, building and previewing that route is worth more this week than any backfill of this file.

Recommendation: park the ingest. Revisit after the 2026-10-24 marathon, when surface-mix and route-suggestion features are on the roadmap. If someone does build it, key on a geometry hash (not courseName), dedupe the 4 known pairs, and store derived distance explicitly flagged as PLANNED so it can never leak into a load calculation.
